#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.

<to_controller>Confirmed: it was names. `grown_at` compared symbols against `Grown.at` and `Arena.node_at` in three places: the body's own inference (item_lowered), the callers' lend-through (`calls_grown`/`grown_lending`) and the memory pass (`grown_at(b.name)`). Fixed in ee0ac7b1, on lent-59 after 40d33cc1:
- **The mark:** `@std/meta` gains `@grown_read`.
- **What counts:** a body lends through its own cell only if it wears the mark AND is a method of an `@opaque` type's own impl, in the file that declares the type (`reads_grown`). There alone are the cells reached. A mark anywhere else lends nothing.
- **Callers:** each callee's declaration is asked through the `CalledFn` the unit lowered (`called_grown` → `signed_body` → `reads_grown`). That's a declaration fact, so a body's lowering still reads no other body's marks.
- **Memory pass:** reads `Body.grown_read`, carried from the lowered fn.
- **Holders:** `Grown.at` and `Arena.node_at` wear the mark; `grown_at` and its two constants are deleted.
- **Witness** (tools/grown_read_witness.sh, uncommitted until it runs): a new holder `Shelf<T>`, written only with `@opaque` and `@grown_read`, must lend, with `avra_grown_view` in its caller's IR. The same holder without the mark, or without `@opaque`, must not. All three must print `2 b1 swapped 7` natively and under eval.
- **Process slip:** I started editing while 40d33cc1's proof was still running in the same tree. I stopped it, and I'm counting none of its results. Its RC-guarded grown_test was also killed for lack of memory, so the guard run will get a smaller pool.
Building gen-1 and gen-2 now (net off), then the witness, then the lent and grown tests, the sound check and the census.</to_controller>

message.content: Lead: check one thing before the census: "`grown_at` names `Arena.node_at` beside `Grown.at`". If the memory pass decides which fns lend by matching their NAMES, that breaks a CLAUDE.md rule ("no string tags or string-matching to detect behavior"), and the next grow-only holder would silently not lend. A lender has to be known by what it IS: a mark on the fn (an annotation, or a `lent` answer mark the signature carries), or derived from the body (it answers a read of an @opaque grow-only cell). If it's names today, make it a mark, with a case where a new holder written only with the mark lends.

payload.result:
<to_controller>The lent-59 build fails on one thing: `@derive(Saved)` on `Seating` (core/checking.av:522) "held more than 5242880 bytes", and the derive's missing methods (`written_into`, `read_from`, `folded_into`) cascade from that. Base57 grew `Seating` (`Heard` and others), and lent's `.Opaque` takes it past 5 MiB. std-avrac's manifest already lifts compile-time runs to 10 MiB for exactly this (`[lifted] memory = 10`), and base57's 45bb42c2 makes the program layer honour it. My reading is that `make try` runs with the net on, so the old path checks first and holds every derive to the 5 MiB default. Testing now: the same `make try` with AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0. If it passes, the choice is yours:
(a) Make the old path read `[lifted]` too, a few lines, as 45bb42c2 did for the program layer.
(b) Fold `.Opaque` into `.Sealed`. Same payload; the voice is chosen by the record's mark. No new variant, and the 17 or-list edits revert.
I'd pick (a): the next variant anyone adds would hit the same wall, and the manifest already says what the package needs.</to_controller>

#!/bin/bash
# a65594cf against its parent a991a61d, on a quiet machine: each compiler built gen-2; each builds the cli
# of one fixed source (snapshot a6d0d0a0) cold twice, interleaved, wall and user CPU and the phases it
# names; each built cli then checks std-json cold three times, user CPU.
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_MEM_POOL_MB=12500; unset AVRA_QTRACE
L=/work/lane/a65; mkdir -p $L; V=/work/avra-v
objs() { make build/llvm_wrapper.o build/ffi.o build/std_io.o build/std_io_watch.o build/std_net.o build/std_process.o build/std_time.o build/libavra_runtime.a > $L/objs.log 2>&1; }
for c in a991a61d a65594cf; do
  cd $V; git checkout -q -- .; git checkout -q --detach $c; find packages/cli/.avra-cache -delete 2>/dev/null
  objs || { echo "$c objects failed"; exit 1; }
  cp /work/lane/avra-mm build/avra.new && mv build/avra.new build/avra
  make try > $L/$c-g1.log 2>&1 || { echo "$c gen-1 failed"; tail -3 $L/$c-g1.log; exit 1; }
  cp build/avra-try build/avra.new && mv build/avra.new build/avra; sleep 3
  make try > $L/$c-g2.log 2>&1 || { echo "$c gen-2 failed"; tail -3 $L/$c-g2.log; exit 1; }
  cp build/avra-try $L/compiler-$c; echo "$c gen-2 built"
done
cd $V; git checkout -q -- .
# the fixed source, with its own link objects and runtime
S=$L/src; find $S -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p $S; git -C /work/avra archive a6d0d0a0 | tar -x -C $S
cd $S && objs || { echo "fixed source objects failed"; tail -3 $L/objs.log; exit 1; }
for rep in 1 2; do for c in a991a61d a65594cf; do
  cd $S; cp $L/compiler-$c build/avra.new && mv build/avra.new build/avra; sleep 3
  find packages/cli/.avra-cache packages/cli/src/main -delete 2>/dev/null; export AVRA_CACHE_DIR=$L/machine-$c-$rep; find $AVRA_CACHE_DIR -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p $AVRA_CACHE_DIR
  AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_QUERY_TIMES=1 /usr/bin/time -f 'TIME wall %e s user %U s sys %S s rss %M KB' build/avra build --time packages/cli > $L/build-$c-$rep.out 2>&1
  echo "$c build $rep: $(grep '^TIME' $L/build-$c-$rep.out) | $(grep -m1 '^time:' $L/build-$c-$rep.out | cut -c1-150)"
  [ $rep = 1 ] && cp packages/cli/src/main $L/cli-$c
done; done
for rep in 1 2 3; do for c in a991a61d a65594cf; do
  cd $S; cp $L/cli-$c build/avra.new && mv build/avra.new build/avra; sleep 3

  echo "$c check std-json $rep: $(grep '^TIME' $L/check-$c-$rep.out)"
done; done

1. **Compilers:** build each commit twice, gen-2, so both compilers are built by their own code generation and the comparison is fair.

3. **Output speed:** the cli each compiler produced does a cold `check packages/std-json`, three runs each, user CPU.

Checking what `AVRA_QUERY_TIMES` prints, so I know which lines are the emit and LLVM time.

Author: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

    A value of parts is held and passed as its leaves; a level-0 object answers one through a lent pointer
    
    The emitter held a record, a tagged pair or a maybe as one first-class LLVM
    aggregate, which the fast instruction selector selects nowhere: at a seat, an
    answer, a phi, a store or an insertvalue each went to the slow one. A register of
    parts is now held as its leaf scalars: packs and extracts are list operations,
    phis, loads and stores go leaf by leaf (by struct GEP, so the memory layout is
    unchanged), and a call passes each leaf as a seat. A level-0 object answers a
    value of parts through a pointer the caller lends; every other level answers in
    registers, and the opt level is part of every object's key. A part no element
    fills is zero, never undef. No runtime or extern row moves. A call answering
    nothing takes its context from its block, so an indirect one no longer reads a
    global it has none of. tools/level_mix_attack.sh builds one package at level 0,
    level 2 beside it, level 0 again and released.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
    Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01F8zAGciMYsySfVzanrQ8kW

 }

+/// `AVRA_QUERY_FAMILIES=all`: each process names every family it timed, in milliseconds, where it

+fn families_whole() -> bool { families_asked() == "all" }

+    // LICENSED input.debug_flag: a timing's width, which no answer reads

+

-    "core ${core}: ${answered} answered; time: ${times.spoken(15)}; split: ${times.split()}; ${waits_said()}"
+    "core ${core}: ${answered} answered; time: ${if families_whole() { times.spoken_whole() } else { times.spoken(15) }}; split: ${times.split()}; ${waits_said()}"
 }

I have the full mechanism. `digest_of_binary` (build.av:416) does `read_bytes(at)` on the whole ~100 MB binary and digests it in memory. So any run whose compiler binary was written within 2 s holds the binary on the heap, and the next run repeats it until one run outside the window writes the record. That explains the 190 MB. It also explains the tracked `packages/cli/src/.main.print` that moved during the gate: it is this record, stamp plus absolute path plus digest, beside the cli's own built binary.

<to_controller>The 190 MB first-edit spike is explained, deterministic and pre-existing.
- **Repro:** place a compiler (`cp X build/avra.new && mv …`, a new file), run a cold check within 2 s, then an edited check. The edited check peaks at 190 MB every time. With a 3 s wait after placing the binary: 9 MB, every time (9/190/9, 190/9/190/9).
- **Mechanism:** `own_print` (cli disk_host.av:166) keys every kept artifact by a digest of the compiler binary's bytes. It caches that digest in a record beside the binary, keyed by the binary's stamp. Inside the 2 s window `stamp()` withholds, so the run digests the bytes and writes no record, and the next run digests again. `digest_of_binary` (std-avrac build.av:416) does `read_bytes` on the whole ~100 MB binary, which is the peak.
- **What's wrong:** the re-read itself is the stated design ("the bytes are read again when … the host cannot tell"). Holding the binary on the heap isn't necessary.
- **Proposed fix (batch 59, small):** digest the binary through a mapping, std-program already has `avra_mmap_open`, or stream it in chunks. The window case then costs a read, not ~190 MB live. Witness: the repro above, with peak live within noise of the 3 s case.
- **Related:** the tracked `packages/cli/src/.main.print` that the gate rewrote is this very record (stamp, absolute path, digest) for the cli's own built binary. It shouldn't be tracked; I suggest untracking and ignoring it in the same change.
- **Status:** Q ask's four-build spread is still running. Shall I take the mmap digest for 59?</to_controller>

Most of the differences go both ways and sit in byte totals: text lengths, slices, joins. That is what happens when two binaries carry different code hashes. Hash texts change length, and hash-keyed tables probe differently, so their list reads shift too. The only rows `Q ask` itself explains are `once: 598 → 599 reads, 1369 → 1375 pointer compares`: the flag is read once and checked at its sites. To separate the two, I'll take the noise floor between two equivalent builds whose code hashes differ. The frontier-58 lane's g0 and g3 builds give exactly that, and the `Q ask` difference must fall inside it.

<to_controller>Q ask zero-cost census, 67c7660a against 412a2199, flag off, snapshot 53e67752:
- **Warm rows:** identical on every edit row (added 286, added_after 79, body 45, comment 44, inline 61, literal 44, noop 0, signature 68), and every per-query count is the same.
- **Cold census:** not byte-identical. retains −32,598 (−0.001 %), list reads +4.30 M (+0.03 %), boxes −1,791, and byte totals in text/slice rows move both ways.
- **Q ask's own cost:** `once` 598 → 599 reads (the flag read once) and 1,369 → 1,375 pointer compares. No string is built.
- **Likely source of the rest:** the binaries' code hashes differ, so the hash texts and the hash-keyed table probes differ.
- **Before I call it zero:** I'll measure the same rows between two equivalent hash-moving builds (g0/g3 on frontier-58, already queued), and the Q ask difference must fall inside that floor. If it doesn't, I'll move the flag into an engine field read at construction.</to_controller>

<to_controller>Container restart: the witness run was lost partway, but its first numbers survived, and they show a real defect P4 introduced.
- **What survived:** new compiler, one-program store 8 MB peak; many-package store (1,073 MB) 48 MB peak, 306 MB RSS. Base56 one-program 8 MB.
- **Cause:** the store evicts frontier files by print (`prints_evicted`, KEPT_FRONTIERS = 2), ranked by newest pack generation. Scoped frontiers didn't carry the binary's pack print, so every program's frontier counted as a foreign binary with generation 0, and all but one were evicted. The shared store held exactly one frontier file. std-json found none and settled ~38k questions from records: 42 MB peak, against 3 MB over its own store, in the same edited warm check.
- **Fix, 67c7660a:** a scoped frontier is named `<binary print>~<program hash>` (`scoped_print` / `binary_of` in answer_record), so eviction keeps or drops it with its binary. Compaction's `frontier_seeds` keeps alive the questions of every frontier of the binary, whatever program it is scoped to.
- **New case:** four programs share one store, and each one's next process works nothing out and checks no record. It fails against the old eviction and passes on the fix.
- **Bundle:** a4aeef03 (hash order), 5da4eda2 (per-program frontier + flat readers), 67c7660a (eviction).

C=$1; tag=$2; W=/work/avra-w; cd $W
cp "$C" build/avra.new && mv build/avra.new build/avra
src=packages/std-json/src/json.av; cp $src /work/lane/p4w-json.orig
target=std-json
fill="std-text std-time std-validate std-sql std-queue std-task std-toml std-url std-http std-ui std-cli std-relation std-program std-avrac"
link_all() {  # every package's checks kept at $1 ($2 = only the target)
  for p in packages/*/; do
    find "$p.avra-cache" -maxdepth 0 -type l -delete 2>/dev/null
    [ -L "$p.avra-cache" ] || find "$p.avra-cache" -delete 2>/dev/null
  done
  for p in packages/*/; do n=$(basename $p); { [ -z "$2" ] || [ "$n" = "$2" ]; } && { mkdir -p "$1/$n"; ln -s "$1/$n" "$p.avra-cache"; mkdir -p "$1/$n/tapes"; find "$1/$n/tapes" -maxdepth 0 -delete; ln -s "$1/shared" "$1/$n/tapes" 2>/dev/null; }; done
  mkdir -p "$1/shared"
}
# the warm check after one edit of the target's source, so its frontier is walked; the edit put back after
edited_peak() { printf '\n// witness edit\n' >> $src; sleep 3; peak $target; cp /work/lane/p4w-json.orig $src; sleep 3; peak $target > /dev/null; }
peak() { AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 /usr/bin/time -f 'rss %M KB %e s' build/avra check packages/$1 2>&1 >/dev/null | grep -E '^mem: peak|^rss' | tr '\n' ' '; }
S=/work/lane/p4w-$tag; find $S -delete 2>/dev/null
link_all $S/one $target
peak $target > /dev/null; echo "$tag one-program warm after an edit: $(edited_peak) frontier files $(find $S/one -name '*.frontier*' -o -name '*.base' -o -name '*.delta' | wc -l)"
link_all $S/many
for p in $fill; do peak $p > /dev/null; done
peak $target > /dev/null; echo "$tag many-package warm after an edit: $(edited_peak) store $(du -sm $S/many/shared | cut -f1) MB"
for p in packages/*/; do find "$p.avra-cache" -maxdepth 0 -type l -delete 2>/dev/null; done

frontier: one frontier per program, its walk sized by the program

A store many programs share held one frontier for every program a binary
checked: reading it, for one program, walked every place each of them had
ever reached. spec-harness measured a warm check over a tree-wide store at
5,059 MB live against 209 MB over the program's own.

The frontier is now known by the binary's print and the program the engine
asks for (`query_engine(store, definitions, program)`, `frontier_print`), so
a program reads and writes only its own; the packs stay shared, so another
program's answers are still found by their records. Every cli engine names
its package; the work-ahead engine takes its asker's.

readers_of no longer holds a list per place: the readers deltas wrote are
laid flat in two lists of numbers, and the second pass reads each place's
readers again rather than keeping them.

payload.result:
The decide-every-reached-place rule (a4aeef03) gives the same rows as the first fix: 286 / 12, 79, and the rest identical across f0/f3/f4. So the warm rows are now deterministic, but they sit at the top of the old noise range, not the luckiest order's 280/76. My earlier claim that the canonical set is "never wider" holds for the reached set (the unit test shows 10 against 12/14), but not for `worked`. I'll report that as it is.

<to_controller>a4aeef03 on the warm lane (snapshot 53e67752), three builds that move hashes: f0, f3 and f4 all give edit-added 286 with seats_written 12, added_after 79, body 45, comment 44, inline 61, literal 44, noop 0, signature 68. Identical, so the hash-order noise is gone. Correction to my "narrower, never wider": that holds for the reached set (10 against 12/14 in the unit test), but `worked` settles at base56's worst order (286/79), not its luckiest (280/76). The lucky orders did fewer cut decisions, and a decision can cost a compute where a record check would have done. Whether a canonical rule can match 280 is open; I'll look at it after P4, unless you'd rather take determinism at 286 as the new baseline.

P4 folded in (uncommitted, builds next):
(a) Store-wide frontier: the frontier is keyed by `frontier_print()`, the hash of the print plus the program name. `query_engine(store, defs, program = "")`; every cli engine site passes `disk.name`, and the work-ahead engine takes `asking.program`. A store shared by many programs then holds one frontier per program, and a program reads only its own. Packs stay shared.
(b) `readers_of` no longer allocates a boxed list per place. The overlay readers are laid flat (two int lists, counting-sort), and pass two re-reads each place's readers instead of keeping `next` lists. That was the 3 GB over 588 buffers. Frontier tests 63/64, the one failure being the listed sandbox case.
Witness plan: one target package, checked warm over a one-program store and over a store where every package's .avra-cache/tapes is symlinked to one directory and filled first. Peak live (AVRA_MEM_STATS) is measured on the old and new compilers; the old must blow up and the new must match within noise. Not yet scoped: the store-wide stamps file (input_stamps reads every stamp). If the witness shows it, it's next.</to_controller>

The same check, warm over a store holding only its own program: 209 MB live / 204 s. Warm over a shared tree store holding every package: 5,059 MB / 18 GB RSS / 339 s. Top sites: Frontier.readers_of (one list grown to 3 GB over 588 buffers), frontier.overlay (~1.1 GB), stale_places 462 MB, hash_keyed_table slots_holding 429 MB. The law: a frontier's walk visits only places the asking program's questions reach (scoped by print or by the program's roots), so its cost is the program's, whatever else the store holds. Your two-pass closure must hold to that too. Witness: the same check warm over a one-program store and over a many-package store, at the same live peak within noise. The tree-wide store (reverted from batch 57 for now) returns once this holds.

The fix is committed on branch `frontier-order` as 26c162a7. The new test fails on the old walk and passes on the new one. The heavy proofs are queued behind the running base56 control.

<to_controller>Frontier fix built: frontier-order 26c162a7, off the lane head 67823487, no lent and no Grown.
- **Change:** `readers_of` first finds the full reader closure of `changed`, then settles each place in reading order, once all its reads inside the closure are settled. A place that read a moved place is decided: STANDS cuts it, MOVED reaches it and marks it moved, NOT_CUT reaches it. A place that read only reached places is reached undecided. The result depends only on the graph and the answers; if the readers go round, it is null (the frontier is unusable).
- **New test** frontier_order_test, one graph under eight code spellings, i.e. eight place orders:
  - Old walk: fails. Reached is 12 under six orders and 14 under two.
  - Fixed walk: 3/3. Reached is 10 under every order, and the work is identical (text 4, length 2, echo 2, measured 2, steady 2, shown 0, through 2).
  - Every warm answer equals the cold process's.
  - The attack: `through` is a cut that a change reaches only through `echo`, which doesn't cut, so `echo` is merely reached. It is still worked out (through:2), so nothing that should rework is skipped. I read "must still be decided" as "must be worked out": it is reached, and settled when asked. It doesn't go through decide(), because nothing it reads moved for certain.
- **Queued after the base56 v3/v4 control:** gate edit-a..g (witness_program_edit, warm == cold), the std-program suite and the gate's cost slice. Then the warm lane on three builds of the fix that move code hashes, to check every edit row is identical. After that: land it alone, rebase lent/Grown on it, re-measure.</to_controller>

#!/bin/sh
# THE GATE, IN SLICES: every receipt a landing is held to, cut into slices that each run alone in a
# tree of their own, so N machines run N slices at once and the gate takes as long as its longest
# slice. A slice builds the compiler of HEAD itself when build/avra was built from anything else,
# runs every row on the program layer, the net off but where a row's claim is the net, empties the
# stores a cold row reads, bounds every command, keeps each row's words under build/gate/<slice>/, and
# ends with ONE line:
#   GATE <slice> <sha8> PASS|FAIL rows=<n> failed=<n> <seconds>s
# exiting 0 on PASS, 1 on FAIL.
#
#   sh tools/gate.sh list               each slice, one a line, with what it holds
#   sh tools/gate.sh <slice> [arg]      one slice; the idioms slices take the base sha their diff starts at
#   sh tools/gate.sh seed               build/gate/compiler-<sha8>.tar.gz: HEAD's compiler — ONE generation, built
#                                       here first where none of HEAD's stands — and every object a tree
#                                       links with; `pack` is its other name. Run it once; every slice
#                                       then starts from `unpack` and builds nothing.
#   sh tools/gate.sh unpack <file>      seeds this tree from a pack, and holds its stamp to HEAD's: a
#                                       seeded slice builds no compiler
#
# A test row runs every suite (AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1), so it names every failing case, never only the first.
#
# GATE_OLD_PATH=0 drops every row that compares against the old path (they read AVRA_PROGRAM=0);
# when the old path goes, its default goes to 0 and those rows go with one line each.
set -u
root=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$root" || exit 1
unset AVRA_PROGRAM AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE
export AVRA_SUITE_ALL=1
# THE NET IS OFF unless a row's claim is the net: the old path's check before every program-layer
# compile doubles what each row costs and proves nothing a row here asks of it. The rows that keep it
# (AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=1) are the ones that count what it says: the build slice's net-on cli builds and
# their "program-layer false refusal" count, the findings slices' build of every package, held to that
# same count, and the cli's suite, which holds the words a user meets through a child build/avra (at
# slice_cli). `tapes --findings` passes no door, so the net never stood in it.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0

OLD_PATH=${GATE_OLD_PATH:-1}
# the bound of one row, and of a compiler build
ROW_SECS=${GATE_ROW_SECS:-2400}
# every `test` row's failing NAMES are held to tools/gate/<package>.names, the cases a sandbox fails
fmt        fmt --check on every .av the diff from <base> changes (tools/fmt_changed.sh); <base> is the program landed last, never a batch's own base
sound      AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1 check packages/cli, the memory pass's proof run over the program, 0 defects; AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 build packages/cli, every emitted fn verified
cost       make cost: the census compiler, cold, over tools/cost.baseline's snapshot; every count within 0.05% of its row
doors-a    test std-json std-task std-validate std-text std-sql std-queue std-time
doors-b    test std-ui std-http; make ui-host-test and ui-host, std-ui's program tests built and run
findings-a tapes --findings on std-avrac and cli, 0 refusals; std-avrac built, 0 program-layer false refusals
findings-b the same on a third of every other package, dealt in turn
findings-c the next third
findings-d the last third
refusal-a  witness_program_refusal over a third of its cases, dealt in turn
refusal-b  the next third
refusal-c  the last third
witness-b  witness_program_runs, heir_save_attack, share_merge_attack, wave_share_attack, beside_attack, level_mix_attack, _ledger, _suites, _doors; witness_program_differential; make flow-trace; witness_compiler_key; docs_cache_attack, obj_gone_attack, moved_tree_attack, layer_sites_attack, closure_gather_attack, store_bound_attack, path_leak_attack, case_leftover_attack, witness_program_fixes, root_listing_attack, two_compilers_attack
warnings-a witness_program_warnings — the cli built cold and again with no change, on both paths
warnings-b witness_program_warnings — the cli's check on both paths, and the cases under tools/program-warnings/
warnings-c witness_program_warnings — the cli edited, built warm on the program layer
edit-a     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY="embed infer composed gathered"
edit-b     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=1
edit-c     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=5
edit-d     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=10
edit-e     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=rename
edit-f     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-whole
edit-g     witness_program_edit, WITNESS_ONLY=modes-layered
EOF
}

# whether build/avra was built from this tree's compiler source: the stamp's hash of that source, the
# commit it stood at aside — a commit that moves no compiler source moves no compiler
compiler_stands() {
    [ -x build/avra ] && [ "$(cut -d' ' -f1 build/.avra-built-from 2>/dev/null)" = "$(sh tools/work built-from . | cut -d' ' -f1)" ]
}

# what a built tree holds that a fresh one needs to stand as built: the compiler, its hot leaves, its
# stamp, and every object, archive, library, content stamp and dependency list build/ keeps at its top
packed() {
    for f in build/avra build/avra_hot.bc build/avra_hot.inc build/.avra-built-from; do [ ! -f "$f" ] || echo "$f"; done
    find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name '*.sha' -o -name '*.d' \) | sort
}

# a tree seeded from the pack `$1`, or left as it was: a pack is proved whole first — gzip's own check,
# a listing to its end, the compiler and its stamp in it — and refused when its stamp is not this
tools/witness_program_edit.sh:29:#   sh tools/witness_program_edit.sh [compiler]   (default build/avra-try, built
tools/witness_program_edit.sh:42:[ -x "$avra" ] || { echo "witness_program_edit: no compiler at $avra" >&2; exit 1; }
tools/witness_program_edit.sh:81:    made() { "$avra" build "$pkg" >"$tmp/log" 2>&1 || { echo "witness_program_edit: the embedded build failed:" >&2; tail -5 "$tmp/log" >&2; exit 1; }; unsigned_at "$pkg/src/main" "$1" ""; }
tools/witness_program_edit.sh:90:    cmp -s "$tmp/embedded.warm" "$tmp/embedded.cold" || { echo "witness_program_edit: after the embedded file's edit the warm product is not the cold one" >&2; exit 1; }
tools/witness_program_edit.sh:91:    cmp -s "$tmp/embedded.cold" "$tmp/embedded.base" && { echo "witness_program_edit: the embedded file's edit moved nothing" >&2; exit 1; }

payload.result:
The order dependence is in `Frontier.readers_of` (frontier.av:448-477). It's a stack walk that marks a place `reached` the first time it pops. A reader met first from a merely suspect place is pushed undecided and never gets `decide` (so it never cuts), and its readers inherit "suspect". Met first from a moved place, the same reader is decided: if it stands it cuts, if it moved its readers get decided too. Both the suspect set and the cut work done therefore depend on pop order, which is place order, which is hash order.

<to_controller>Design for the frontier fix (control still running):
(1) The order dependence is in `Frontier.readers_of` (frontier.av:448): its DFS stack marks a place reached on first pop. A reader first met from a merely suspect place is never decided; met first from a moved place, it is decided and may cut. So the suspect set and the cut work (counted in `worked`) follow pop order, which is place order, which is hash order.
(2) Fix: two passes. First the plain reader closure of `changed`, ignoring cuts. Then a walk of that closure in topological order (Kahn: a place goes only after every read of it inside the closure is settled), so each place sees the final state of all its reads.
(3) Canonical rule per place r: if r has at least one moved read (changed or CUT_MOVED) and its query cuts, decide(r). STANDS means r is not a suspect, because it was just worked fresh. MOVED means suspect and moved. Otherwise, if any read is a suspect, r is a suspect without being decided. Same graph and same answers give the same set and the same decide calls, whatever the order.
(4) The tie-break among ready places is by place only for determinism, and the result can't depend on it. Who computes a shared child first then changes nothing recorded (one compute, the same reads), so `worked` is fixed.
(5) Proof: a std-program test running readers_of on a permuted copy of one graph and asserting the same reached set and decide set; then A/B and probe variants with identical `worked` on every edit row, plus the warm-row cost gate. Any difference against today is a narrower suspect set (fewer reworks), never a wider one.</to_controller>

That may be part of batch 57's warm rise, which wrong-answers is bisecting now. Fix direction: the cut decisions are order-independent, with an owner chosen canonically (e.g. the read's own stable key, or the earliest asker by item order, never by question hash). payload.result:
Found the mechanism, pending the control.

- **Input checks** (query_engine.av:546): `frontier_opened` checks the standing inputs in place order.
- **Cut decisions** (query_engine.av:604-627): `suspects_of` calls `f.readers_of(changed, cut_at)` and settles each cutting answer in place order.
- **Place order is question-hash order** (frontier.av:836-854). A question's hash includes its code hash.

So whichever cutting question comes first in hash order computes the shared reads, such as `file_scope` against `file_items`, and its record owns them. That changes what the next edit reaches. Waiting on base56 v3 and v4 to see whether this predates lent.

<to_controller>A/B with `Q ask`: adding the line again made B 280 (A 280, B 280). The ask order differs, though: the first root asks are A [language_print, source_text, file_scope→computes file_items] and B [source_text, language_print, file_items computed as a root]. The mechanism: the frontier checks its inputs (frontier_opened) and decides its cuts (suspects_of → readers_of → cut_at) in place order, and place order is question-hash order (frontier.av places_in_order / sorted_by_hash). A question's hash includes the code hash of the lowered code its query reaches. So any change in reachable lowered code reorders the cut decisions. That changes which question computes a shared read and owns it in its record, and so what a later edit reaches: 280 vs 286. The lent reorder changes lowered code, and so does every probe I add, which is why the probes flip it. The base56 control could not see this: an unused fn is not reached, and swapping two whole fns leaves the digest the same, so no hash moved. Running the proper control now: base56 with equivalent edits that do move hashes (disjunct order inside `closes` and `turns`, which are reached). I expect the defect predates lent: warm `worked` depends on code-hash order.</to_controller>

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, then the command the census compiler runs in the snapshot.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli check --counts packages/cli
EOF
}

# THE WARM RE-RUN WORK OF AN EDIT: over the store the cold cli check left, `tapes --findings` of the
# cli is settled; then each edit of one file is made, the findings run warm and the answers it worked
# out again kept (its `worked:` line), and the file put back and the findings warmed back, so each edit
# meets the store the one before it left. The edits and their file are the warm lane's measured
# table's, so a row reads against its design budget.
# kind|text|what it becomes, `\n` between lines; a noop edits nothing.
edited=packages/cli/src/commands/cache.av
edits() {
    cat << 'EOF'
noop||
inline|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a directory of immutable packs, each the|//! in, its own verbs. The store is a folder of immutable packs, each the
literal|    println("avra cache clean: ${compacted_said(dir)}")|    println("avra cache cleaned: ${compacted_said(dir)}")
comment|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    // a note\n    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }
body|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }|    let shared? = machine_layer() else { return 0 }\n    let _ = cache_dir().length
signature|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int {|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>, most: int = 0) -> int {
added|fn cache_dir() -> string {|fn cache_unused() -> int { 3 }\n\nfn cache_dir() -> string {
added_after|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }|fn octets_of(packs: List<PackListed>) -> int { packs.fold(0, (sum, p) -> sum + p.octets) }\n\nfn spare_one() -> int { 1 }
EOF
}

mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
compiler=${COST_COMPILER:-build/avra.census}
if [ -z "${COST_COMPILER:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$compiler"
fi
[ -x "$compiler" ] || { echo "cost: no census compiler at $compiler"; exit 1; }

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    touch -d '1 hour ago' "$src/$edited"
    if [ "$1" = edit-added ]; then export AVRA_QTRACE=1; fi
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    unset AVRA_QTRACE
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }
}

# Each edit of the warm lane's table, over the store the cli check left.
warm_edits() {
    warm settle
    cp "$src/$edited" "$out/edited.orig"
    edits | while IFS='|' read -r kind text becomes; do
        [ -z "$text" ] || python3 "$root/tools/cost_ratchet.py" --edit "$src/$edited" "$kind" "$text" "$becomes"
        warm "edit-$kind"
        if [ -n "$text" ]; then
            cp "$out/edited.orig" "$src/$edited"
            warm "back-$kind"
        fi
    done
    find "$out/settle.out" "$out"/back-*.out -delete
}

bare() {
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache"
    find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete
}

workloads | while read -r name command; do
    bare
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    counted "$name" $command
    [ "$name" != check-cli ] || warm_edits
done
find "$out/cache" "$src" "$out/edited.orig" -delete

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

     - `make try` builds build/avra-try using the standing build/avra.

     - The program-layer QueryEngine (std-program) and the relation engine (std-relation).

content.content:
mkdir -p "$out"
find "$out" -mindepth 1 -delete
compiler=${COST_COMPILER:-build/avra.census}
if [ -z "${COST_COMPILER:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$compiler"
fi
[ -x "$compiler" ] || { echo "cost: no census compiler at $compiler"; exit 1; }

src=$out/src
mkdir -p "$src/build"
git archive "$snapshot" | tar -x -C "$src"
cp "$compiler" "$src/build/avra"
find build -maxdepth 1 -type f \( -name '*.o' -o -name '*.a' -o -name '*.so' -o -name 'avra_hot.bc' -o -name 'avra_hot.inc' \) \
    -exec cp {} "$src/build/" \;
printf '%s\n' "$snapshot" > "$out/snapshot"
cache=$root/$out/cache

# One run of the census compiler in the snapshot, once what it reads is older than the stamp window:
# its census to <name>.out, what it printed to <name>.stdout.
counted() {
    name=$1; shift
    sleep 3
    started=$(date +%s)
    # the census reports at exit only where the run accounts (AVRA_MEM_STATS)
    (cd "$src" && AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$cache" AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 \
        sh "$root/tools/memcap.sh" "${COST_CAP_MB:-8000}" taskset -c 0 build/avra "$@" \
        > "$root/$out/$name.stdout" 2> "$root/$out/$name.out") || {
        tail -20 "$out/$name.out"; echo "cost: $name failed ($*)"; exit 1; }
    echo "cost: $name $(($(date +%s) - started)) s"
}

# One warm findings run of the cli, its `worked:` line kept as <name>.out, its census beside it.
warm() {
    counted "$1" tapes --findings packages/cli
    mv "$out/$1.out" "$out/$1.census"
    grep '^worked: ' "$out/$1.census" > "$out/$1.out" || { echo "cost: $1 printed no worked line"; exit 1; }
}
workloads | while read -r name command; do
    bare
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    counted "$name" $command
    [ "$name" != check-cli ] || warm_edits
done
find "$out/cache" "$src" "$out/edited.orig" -delete

The warm row edit-added worked 280 → 286 (seats_written 6 → 12) is caused by ONE semantically equivalent reorder in memory.av `lent_answer`: checking `marks.any(it.lent)` before building the per-seat list instead of after. Runs: HEAD 280; HEAD + an unused fn 280; HEAD + that reorder 286, deterministic over repeat runs. So the warm-edit row moves with a change that cannot change any answer. Either the compiler built through lent miscompiles somewhere, so early cutoff misses, or the warm lane has a timing edge (cost.sh's 2-second stamp window). I've dropped the reorder (it buys nothing) and am rerunning the full gate. Next I'll trace both binaries with AVRA_QTRACE over the edit-added step to name which seats_written asks differ. Separately, the list-read rise (+1.75%) is Grown's hop; the fix is Arena = { ..Grown<N>, … } (@opaque, no hop), after this run.</to_controller>

The full cost rerun is in progress.

# Each edit of the warm lane's table, over the store the cli check left.
warm_edits() {
    warm settle
    cp "$src/$edited" "$out/edited.orig"
    edits | while IFS='|' read -r kind text becomes; do
        [ -z "$text" ] || python3 "$root/tools/cost_ratchet.py" --edit "$src/$edited" "$kind" "$text" "$becomes"
        warm "edit-$kind"
        if [ -n "$text" ]; then
            cp "$out/edited.orig" "$src/$edited"
            warm "back-$kind"
        fi
    done
    find "$out/settle.out" "$out"/back-*.out -delete
}

bare() {
    find "$src" -path '*/.avra-cache*' -delete
    find "$src/packages" \( -path '*/src/main' -o -name '*.av.ll' \) -type f -delete
    mkdir -p "$cache"
    find "$cache" -mindepth 1 -delete
}

workloads | while read -r name command; do
    bare
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    counted "$name" $command
    [ "$name" != check-cli ] || warm_edits
done

collection, then act on the snapshot. pool.av's `reap` is the
      exemplar: it reads `stale`, sets `kept` to the survivors, and only
      then closes each stale carrier. Not ratcheted: no grep tells a park
      from any other call.

- net.world_waited_by_read (unratcheted) A TEST WAITS ON THE WORLD WITH A
      PARKED READ, NEVER WITH A SLEEP. A case runs on the virtual clock,
      where a sleep with no descriptor parked takes no time; a close
      reaches its peer in the kernel's time — at once on Linux loopback,
      a moment later on macOS. THE SMELL: `sleep(…)` then a one-shot poll
      of the peer (`try_read(…) is .Eof`, a `.Pending -> false` arm).
      THE IDIOM: read the peer to its end with parked reads under a
      deadline (`within secs(2) { … c.read(…) … }`), the end read being
      the fact. Not ratcheted: whether a sleep is free depends on what
      other tasks have parked, which no grep sees, and a test reading
      `try_read`'s `.Eof` or `.Pending` is also how std-net proves
      `try_read` itself.

content.content:
## The idiom registry

This file is the RULEBOOK of the future idiom engine (ROADMAP, Era
IV): every entry below is a lint rule being written by hand. The
mechanically-greppable subset is ENFORCED today by the ratchet
(`make idioms`, wired into the gate — smells may never rise;
deliberate exceptions bump `tools/idioms.baseline` in the same
commit). When a review round or a milestone discovers a NEW idiom,
it lands here AT DISCOVERY, with its smell, its licensed
exceptions, and — where greppable — a ratchet rule.

THE BAR rests on five laws, and the first three exist because the
old ratchet had a hole under each. Every idiom the language can
state is a `rule` declaration now, found by `avra check` itself
(compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av) — `tools/idioms.py`,
the regex tool this section originally described, is gone, ported
out to the last shape (avra-8sb5.25.16); `tools/idioms.baseline` and
`avra check --baseline` (wired into `make idioms`/`make idioms-accept`)
carry the five laws below now.

  1. THE BASELINE LISTS SITES, NEVER COUNTS. The old tool compared
     totals, so fixing one smell while adding another passed
     silently — a net-zero swap. Now a new site fails on its own.
  2. NO TOOL PATH ADDS TO THE BASELINE. `--accept` only PRUNES what
     is gone, so the debt can only fall. The old escape hatch was
     "bump the pinned number", which is how a ratchet becomes
     theatre: style.accumulator_declaration drifted 39 -> 41 -> 40 -> 41 -> 43 across four
     milestones, each bump self-licensed in its own commit.
  3. A LICENSE LIVES AT THE SITE: `// LICENSED loops.push_loop: a ZIP of
     parallel captures`. The reason sits where the code is,
     forever, instead of as an integer nobody reads. A new
     violation therefore has two honest exits — write the
     idiomatic form, or say why it cannot be written.
766:- style.mutable_slot_not_cell (unratcheted) A MUTABLE SLOT IS A `Cell`, NEVER A ONE-ELEMENT
776:- style.encoding_empty_field_dropped (unratcheted) A DELIMITED ENCODING
793:- compiler.publish_by_rename (unratcheted) A PATH OTHER PROCESSES READ IS
809:- http.snapshot_settle_act (unratcheted) A LOOP THAT MAY PARK ACTS ON A
825:- net.world_waited_by_read (unratcheted) A TEST WAITS ON THE WORLD WITH A

#!/bin/sh
# THE EXACT-COUNT GATE'S MEASUREMENT: the census compiler of this tree, run over FIXED workloads whose
# sources are one pinned commit (the `snapshot` row of tools/cost.baseline): cold, each run's census
# kept as build/cost/<workload>.out; and warm after each edit of a fixed set, the answers it worked out
# again kept as build/cost/edit-<kind>.out. tools/cost_ratchet.py judges them.
#   sh tools/cost.sh                      the baseline's snapshot
#   COST_SNAPSHOT=<sha> sh tools/cost.sh  another snapshot (what `make cost-accept` records)
#   COST_COMPILER=<file> sh tools/cost.sh a census compiler already built from this tree
#
# A FIXED INPUT MEASURES THE COMPILER: the snapshot is exported whole, std included, and the census
# compiler stands at its build/avra beside the objects a build links, so every package it reads is
# the snapshot's.
# ONE PROCESS ON ONE CORE DOES ALL THE WORK: a forked worker's counts are its own, so no body is
# lowered ahead (AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF) and the run is held to one core (`taskset`), the width every
# emitter reads, so objects are made in this process by one worker.
# EVERY COLD RUN STARTS BARE: an empty store, and no product a run before it left, which a build reads.
# A FILE IS READ ONLY ONCE IT IS OLDER THAN THE STAMP WINDOW (io.stamp withholds a stamp from a path
# changed in the last two seconds), so what a run stamps never depends on how fast it began.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
root=$(pwd)
out=build/cost
snapshot=${COST_SNAPSHOT:-$(awk '$1 == "snapshot" { print $2 }' tools/cost.baseline 2> /dev/null)}
[ -n "$snapshot" ] || { echo "cost: tools/cost.baseline names no snapshot"; exit 1; }
# A SHALLOW CLONE FETCHES THE ONE COMMIT IT PINS.
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || git fetch -q --depth=1 origin "$snapshot" 2> /dev/null || :
git cat-file -e "$snapshot^{commit}" 2> /dev/null || {
    echo "cost: snapshot $snapshot is not in this clone and could not be fetched"; exit 1; }
command -v taskset > /dev/null || { echo "cost: no taskset to hold the run to one core"; exit 1; }

# The cold workloads: a name, then the command the census compiler runs in the snapshot.
workloads() {
    cat << 'EOF'
check-cli check --counts packages/cli
build-cli build packages/cli
check-program check --counts packages/std-program
EOF
}

# THE WARM RE-RUN WORK OF AN EDIT: over the store the cold cli check left, `tapes --findings` of the

content.content:
**The classifier** is what makes candidates automatic. A census site's SHAPE names its technique:

| site shape (from the census) | technique |
|---|---|
| a box freed in the fn that made it | stack records (escape analysis) |
| a free at rc 1 followed by an alloc of the same size | reuse in place |
| a retain whose release is the binding's last use | move at last use |
| `avra_streq`/name compare callers | interned names |
| a box of flat scalar fields pushed into a list | strided list |
| a slot box over a crossed box (`F?`) | nullable flat record |
| a list made and only walked once | deforestation |
| an indirect call whose target set is one fn | devirtualization |
| a `dyn` box laid with N code pointers | static method tables |

`avra census --candidates` prints the top sites per technique with their counts and the source
line, so a ranked work list is one command. Run per batch on the gate's workloads, its output
diffed against the last run is how a NEW candidate appears without anyone looking.

## How work is assessed

- **Every PR**: the exact-count gate holds; a new shape-rule finding fails like an idiom.
- **Every new feature**: its design post names its cost (boxes, calls, copies per use) and which
  registry rows it relies on or adds. A feature that makes idiomatic code slower needs a row that
  removes the cost, or it is not ready.
- **Maintenance**: a finding from any detector is a row or a ticket at discovery, never a comment.
- **New techniques** join this table with their detector in the same change.

## Techniques

| technique | status | removes |
|---|---|---|
| packed lists of scalars | landed (batch 48) | a mark byte a cell, boxes per element |
| strided lists of flat records | in progress (alloc) | a box per element |
| nullable flat record as presence + words | designed (alloc (2), after the aggregate rewrite) | 2 boxes per `F?` |
| static method tables | done (lowering-quality, to land) | N code-pointer pushes per `dyn` box: one table per type and trait, laid once as data; a box is its value and its table |
| aggregates as leaf scalars, unfilled parts zeroed | done (parallel-main, batch 53) | SelectionDAG fallbacks, undef words |
| store lookup by hash index | done (parallel-main, batch 53) | a binary search per mapped pack per lookup: one probe of each pack's slots instead, about 10 CPU-s of a cold cli build; detector: the census of `span_keyed` / `first_at_or_after` callers (perf: the bodies wave spent 11.3 of 94.7 CPU-s searching 5 packs) |
| release rows | landed (batch 48) | release call sites |
| interned names | proposed | string compares in lookups |
| reuse in place (Perceus/FBIP) | proposed | free + alloc pairs |
| move at last use (borrow inference) | partial (params' consumes) | retain/release pairs |

A list that only grows lends a read of its element: Grown, @opaque, and an outlasting view

`Grown<T>` (core/grown.av) pushes, reads and replaces, and a replaced element is retired, never
dropped, so an element once read stands as long as the list does whatever is written after.
`@opaque` (`@std/meta`) keeps that a law of the type: sealed, and its fields are read only in the
module that declares it — refused on both checkers (`type.opaque`). A `Grown`'s element read is
known by its symbol and lends from its receiver through its cell; a body reading it directly
lends too, its view marked `outlasts`, and a caller reads that view through `avra_grown_view`,
which no call changes — only what lets the holder go: its release, or a call taking it, or a box
it rides, into a consuming seat. The arena's nodes are a `Grown` now, and a store's `expr` and
`stmt` read them directly.

message.content: Lead: approved. Build `Grown<T>` in core: push, at, length, and replace-with-retire, with no set and no pop. Its cell is not reachable from outside the type: keep the field private to core's module, so "only grows" is a law the type holds, not a convention. Arena.nodes (and every other append-only holder the full census names) becomes one. The cross-call lent mark is a marks query with early cutoff, as you said; the warm edit rows must not rise, and the cost gate checks that. Add a ZERO_COST.md row: technique "grow-only holders lend", detector = owned reads of a holder the census names whose type only grows. Land it with the lent machinery (8cdd9cee) as one bundle. Receipts: the census before and after with ROWS_TOP=3000, the sound check at 0, RC-guard clean, eval == native, and an attack where a replaced node's old view is still read after the replace.

<to_controller>(1) NO as stated. `Arena.replaced(i, n)` does `nodes.set_at(i, n)`: 4 sites rewrite nodes (item_canonical.av:91 Verbatim bodies; sugars.av:678/703 renamed idents). It can become a grow: replace-with-retire, where the old box is pushed to a grow-only `retired` list in the arena before `set_at`, so a node box lives as long as the arena whatever is replaced (memory cost: rewrites only, a handful per file). `forked()` shares the list into a new cell; copy-on-write retains every element, so that stays safe. Nothing calls `set` on the cell. (2) Nothing outside arena.av writes an Arena's cells (`.nodes.set/set_at/pop` appear only in arena.av; item_view's `KindNodes.nodes` is a different type). But the type doesn't enforce it: the fields are public. The paradox-collapse shape is a core type `Grown<T>` (a cell list whose only verbs are push, at, length and replace-with-retire; no set, no pop), whose `at` the compiler knows lends from its holder. Arena's `nodes` becomes one, and the law is then by type. (3) Pending: the census's rowcall table stops at its top 30, where node_at (168.6 M) is the only owned read; 767 M of the 936 M owned-read retains are unattributed. Rerunning with AVRA_CENSUS_ROWS_TOP=3000 after the gen-2 suites run in flight. One caveat that stays: node_at is reached through `store.expr/stmt`, so the view still has to cross those calls. That needs a callee's lent mark at the caller, done as a small marks query with early cutoff: callers recompute only when a mark changes, not on every callee edit.</to_controller>

message.content:
Lead: good design, but consider the paradox-collapse version first, because the window analysis pays a cross-body fact for 60% coverage. The arena is APPEND-ONLY: nodes are pushed and never replaced or removed. An element of a grow-only list stays alive for as long as the list does, WHATEVER is written meanwhile. A push may move the buffer, but the element box is held by the list, not by the buffer slot's address. So a read of an existing element from a grow-only holder is a view by its TYPE, with no window and no callee facts. It covers all ~25 sample sites, including the 9 that keep payloads live into writing calls, and the full 169M+169M.
Shape: a type that can only grow (e.g. core `Arena<T>`, or a grow-only Cell: push and read, no set, no set_at, no remove) whose `at(i)` answers a lent view, held by the receiver's own standing. The memory pass needs only "the holder outlives the view", which a borrowed `self` or seat already guarantees.
Check three things:
(1) NodeStore's arenas are truly never replaced whole (`set` on the cell). If they are, can that write become a grow?
(2) Does anything hand out the arena's cell to code that could `set` it?
(3) The census share of all grow-only holders, not just node_at.
If (1) and (2) hold, build that instead of the window. Post the answer to (1)–(3) in a few lines first.

content.text:
By-kind census, base vs lent: lent cut owned-read retains by 52 M (936 → 884 M), but the totals didn't move (2.530 → 2.528 G retains). So the lent machinery alone is noise. The cell case lives in `owned: yielded 0.572 G`, where `node_at`'s 169 M owned gets land; adjacent kinds are "a load that outlives its cell" 0.182 G and "stored in a cell" 0.202 G.

<to_controller>Cell-load design (5 lines):
1. Callee: a body whose answer projects the CURRENT VALUE of a cell reached from seat j (`self.nodes.get()[i]`) gets mark `lent_through_cell[j]`, inferred like `lent` (chain may pass one `Load` of a cell that rides an eligible seat).
2. Caller: such a call's answer is read as a plain view only if, from the call to the last read of the view and of everything derived from it, no step may write any cell: no `Store` to a cell, no cell-writing row (`writes`/`cell_unique`), and no `Call`/`CallPtr` except to a body marked `writes_no_cell`. Cells alias (two fields can hold one cell box), so any write kills; no call also means no fiber switch, so no other task can write. Otherwise it takes the owned twin, as today.
3. `writes_no_cell` is inferred bottom-up from the body's own steps plus its callees' marks; a cycle, `CallPtr` or `dyn` counts as a write.
4. Needed for either: lending THROUGH a call. `node_at` is reached via `store.expr(id)` / `stmt(id)`, so the chain must accept a call to a lending body. That and (3) make inference read CALLEE facts, which neither `consumed` nor `lent` do today: a new cross-body dependency in the program layer, the real cost.
5. Soundness re-derives the window per call site (any cell write inside a lent-through-cell view's life is a defect), and `owned_lent` stays.
Estimate (one-core census, base55 cli build): node_at's owned gets are 169 M retains + 169 M releases, about 5.6% of 6.0 G RC ops (6.7% of retains), all in `owned: yielded`. My sample of 25 `store.expr` sites: ~7 call-free (a scalar-payload match, `is`), ~9 call only a leaf projection method (`text_of`, `body_of`, `elems_of`), ~9 keep a box payload live into calls that write cells. So coverage is ~30% with a call-free window alone (~0.05 G retains + 0.05 G releases) and ~60–65% with leaf `writes_no_cell` (~0.11 G + 0.11 G, ~3.5% of RC ops). Provable: yes, locally per window. Cut: real but modest, and it costs a cross-body fact (4). Plan unless you say otherwise: build (4) + (1) + the call-free window on top of 8cdd9cee, measure, then add `writes_no_cell` only if the measurement holds the estimate.</to_controller>

I've posted the design and estimate. Unless the lead redirects, I'll start on the lend-through-call inference (item 4), since every other part depends on it. First, how inference reaches `lent_seats` today and whether callee marks can reach it:

lent answers: an unwound exit answers nobody, and a lent mark the pass can't keep is a defect

An exit inside the arm an `if` on the unwinding flag opens answers what no caller reads, so
the answer chain skips it — the memory pass and the soundness proof alike. Without that, a
program that unwinds saw every lending body's chain fail at the pass while its callers read
the answer as a view: one count leaked a call, and a compiler built so ran out of memory
lexing one file. The proof now names that shape (`owned_lent`): marks that lend over an
answer counted as owned. A lent read's call answer past the body's old registers owns
nothing too; `nested` pins it.

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS COMPILER: the cli this tree builds, over a runtime compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, written
# to <out>. It counts exactly what the shipping compiler does and never ships: the shipping runtime
# library is rebuilt before this answers, and the cli's own product is gone.
#   sh tools/census_compiler.sh build/avra.census
#
# THE BUILDER IS build/avra unless CENSUS_BUILDER names another: a layout rule is the BUILDING
# compiler's, so a census of a rule builds the census compiler with a compiler that has it.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
out=${1:-build/avra.census}
builder=${CENSUS_BUILDER:-build/avra}
[ -x "$builder" ] || { echo "census: no $builder to build the census compiler with — run \`make avra\` first"; exit 1; }
# A MADE BOX IS NAMED BY ITS CALLER'S CALLER, two frames up, which only frame pointers reach:
# macOS keeps them always, Linux only when asked, in the runtime and in every emitted fn.
counted="-DAVRA_CENSUS -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
shipping() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    find packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll -maxdepth 0 -delete 2> /dev/null || :
}
trap shipping EXIT INT TERM
make --no-print-directory CFLAGS_avra_runtime="$counted" CFLAGS_avra_hot="$counted" build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null
# THE COUNTED LEAVES STAY CALLS: the bitcode the compiler inlines was
# built without the census, so an inlined retain would count nothing.
# THE MINTED BOXES ARE NAMED: each box a runtime row makes is counted by
# its type (AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES), the `type:` table.
# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK: the old path's check the net runs first is not that work.
AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 AVRA_INLINE_RUNTIME=0 AVRA_CENSUS_TYPES=1 AVRA_PROGRAM_MODE=release \
    "$builder" build packages/cli > build/census-build.out 2>&1 || {
    tail -20 build/census-build.out; echo "census: the census compiler did not build"; exit 1; }
# A BINARY THE PROGRAM LAYER PLACES IS ITS KEPT BINARY, LINKED: a census compiler left from an earlier
# run can be that same file, which `mv` will not move onto itself — the old one goes first.
[ ! -e "$out" ] || find "$out" -delete
mv packages/cli/src/main "$out"
# A C symbol wears a leading underscore on macOS and none on Linux.
nm "$out" | grep -Eq '[ _]note_retain$' || { echo "census: $out carries no census — refusing to report"; exit 1; }

    if [ -d "$stores" ]; then rm -rf .avra-cache; mv "$stores" .avra-cache; fi
    for d in $named; do
        if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache"; mv "$d/.avra-cache$suffix" "$d/.avra-cache"; fi
    done
}
trap restore EXIT INT TERM

rm -rf "$stores"
[ -d .avra-cache ] && mv .avra-cache "$stores"
sh tools/census_compiler.sh "$census"

# THE MEASURED RUN STARTS COLD: the census compiler's store is its own
# and was never filled, and the tree's stores stand aside until exit.
# THE FILTER DROPS `mem:`, IT DOES NOT SELECT LABELS: an allowlist of
# census labels is a second registry of them, and goes stale silently.
# A PACKAGE NAMED ON THE COMMAND KEEPS ITS OWN STORE (`tapes <pkg>` writes `<pkg>/.avra-cache`), so it
# stands aside too, or the second census of one package reads the first one's answers.
rm -rf .avra-cache
for d in "$@"; do
    if [ -d "$d/.avra-cache" ]; then rm -rf "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; mv "$d/.avra-cache" "$d/.avra-cache$suffix"; fi
done
if [ -n "${CENSUS_EDIT:-}" ]; then
    sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" > build/census-cold.out 2>&1 || { tail -5 build/census-cold.out; echo "census: the cold run failed"; exit 1; }
    sh -c "$CENSUS_EDIT"
fi
out="$(AVRA_MEM_STATS=1 AVRA_CENSUS_SITES=1 sh tools/memcap.sh "${CENSUS_CAP_MB:-4000}" "$census" "$@" 2>&1 >/dev/null \
    | tee build/census-raw.out | grep -Ev '^(mem:|memcap:)' || true)"
printf '%s\n' "$out" | grep -q '^rc:' || { printf '%s\n' "$out" | tail -5; echo "census: the run printed no counts"; exit 1; }

# THE STORE'S BYTES, read while the census run's own store stands (the exit trap puts the tree's
# back): a row ceiling alone misses rows that got larger.
python3 - <<'PY' > build/census-store.out 2>/dev/null || true
import os
n = 0
for d, _, files in os.walk(".avra-cache/store"):
    n += sum(os.path.getsize(os.path.join(d, f)) for f in files)
print("store: %d bytes" % n)
PY
out="$out
$(cat build/census-store.out 2>/dev/null)"

# Every site's symbol, one line per address in the order given: `atos` on macOS, `addr2line`
# elsewhere, each asked ONCE for all of them — a table of thousands of sites asked one at a time
# spends longer resolving than the census spent counting.
symbols_at() {
    if command -v atos > /dev/null 2>&1; then
        xargs atos -o "$census" 2>/dev/null
    else
        xargs addr2line -f -e "$census" 2>/dev/null | awk 'NR % 2 == 1'
    fi
}

# A SITE IS RESOLVED HERE, while the census binary those addresses

#!/bin/sh
# THE CENSUS BUILD: exact retain/release/list-write counts, and the
# callers that cause them. Counting costs ~8% of a run, so it never
# ships: a census compiler is built BESIDE build/avra, from a runtime
# compiled with -DAVRA_CENSUS, and the shipping runtime library is
# rebuilt on every exit.
#   sh tools/census.sh check packages/std-avrac
#
# THE SHIPPING COMPILER IS NEVER REMOVED. It builds the census
# compiler, so a census that deletes it first has nothing to build
# with, and every recovery that rebuilds needs the memory and disk the
# census run just spent.
#
# CENSUS_EDIT MEASURES A WARM EDIT: the command runs once cold to fill the store,
# then CENSUS_EDIT edits the tree, and only the run after it is counted.
#   CENSUS_EDIT='sh tools/db_measure/edit_literal.sh' sh tools/census.sh check packages/cli
#
# A CENSUS THAT PRINTS NO COUNTS FAILS. A check that examined nothing
# is not a check that passed: no `rc:` line means the binary carried no
# census, and the run exits 1 saying so.
# A cold run clears the tree's `.avra-cache`; the machine store lives there too, or "cold" would read the machine's rows.
export AVRA_CACHE_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)/.avra-cache"
# a store is copied, counted or emptied here between builds, so each build saves its own before it answers
export AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
: "${LLVM_PREFIX:=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm}"
export LLVM_PREFIX

# THE CENSUS COUNTS THE COMPILER'S OWN WORK, under a memory cap: the old path's check the net runs
# before the program layer's is not that work, and its memory with the layer's passes the cap.
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
census=build/avra.census
stores=.avra-cache.census-saved
suffix=.census-saved
named="$*"
restore() {
    make --no-print-directory build/libavra_runtime.a > /dev/null 2>&1 || \
        echo "census: the shipping runtime did NOT rebuild — run \`make build/libavra_runtime.a\`"
    rm -f packages/cli/src/main packages/cli/src/main.av.ll
#!/bin/sh
AVRA_RC_KINDS=1 exec /work/avra-kinds/build/avra-kb "$@"

#!/bin/bash
# proofR.sh <tag> : proof of a change that moves the binary by design (release rows): the new
# compiler's binary held to ITSELF across every way of building, findings held to the base's, a
# self-rebuilt compiler held to a fixed point and run under the RC guard, then the suites and witnesses.
tag=$1; L=/work/lane/proof-$tag; mkdir -p $L
cd /work/avra && . /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
T=$PWD/build/avra-try; B=$PWD/build/avra-base
cold() { find . -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -mindepth 1 -delete \; ; find ~/.avra/cache -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
settle() { while pgrep -x avra-try >/dev/null || pgrep -x avra-base >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli1 >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli0 >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli2 >/dev/null; do sleep 0.3; done; }
findings() { grep -av '^core \|^ahead\|^time:\|^phases:\|^split:\|^kept by\|^within\|^beside' "$1" > "$2"; }
r() { echo "== $*" | tee -a $L/summary; }
same() { cmp packages/cli/src/main $L/try.rel && echo "CMP ok: $1" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "CMP FAIL: $1" | tee -a $L/summary; }
{
r "the dev-built compiler builds the release cli"
#!/bin/sh
# guarded.sh <compiler> <out> : every program test under the features with early exits, errdefer,
# defers and loops built with <compiler>, its binary run under AVRA_RC_GUARD=1, and its output held
# to its .expected; one line a test
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh; export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0 AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1
C=$1; out=$2; : > $out
for exp in $(find /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/fns/tests /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/defers/tests /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/loops/tests /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/results/tests /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/nullable/tests -name '*.expected' | sort); do
  d=$(dirname $exp); n=$(basename $exp .expected); src=$d/$n.av; [ -f $src ] || continue
  w=/tmp/guarded-run/$n; find $w -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p $w; cp $d/*.av $w/ 2>/dev/null
  timeout 200 $C build $w/$n.av > $w/build.log 2>&1 || { echo "$n BUILD-FAIL" >> $out; continue; }
  got=$(cd $w && AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 timeout 30 ./$n 2>&1; echo "status=$?")
  want=$(cat $exp; echo "status=0")
  if [ "$got" = "$want" ]; then echo "$n ok" >> $out; else echo "$n DIFF $(printf '%s' "$got" | tail -2 | tr '\n' ' ' | cut -c1-120)" >> $out; fi
done
