#!/bin/bash
# proofR.sh <tag> : proof of a change that moves the binary by design (release rows): the new
# compiler's binary held to ITSELF across every way of building, findings held to the base's, a
# self-rebuilt compiler held to a fixed point and run under the RC guard, then the suites and witnesses.
tag=$1; L=/work/lane/proof-$tag; mkdir -p $L; : > $L/summary
cd /work/avra && . /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_PROGRAM_NET=0
T=$PWD/build/avra-try; B=$PWD/build/avra-base
cold() { find . -name .avra-cache -type d -prune -exec find {} -mindepth 1 -delete \; ; find ~/.avra/cache -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null; }
settle() { while pgrep -x avra-try >/dev/null || pgrep -x avra-base >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli1 >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli0 >/dev/null || pgrep -x cli2 >/dev/null; do sleep 0.3; done; }
findings() { grep -av '^core \|^ahead\|^time:\|^phases:\|^split:\|^kept by\|^within\|^beside' "$1" > "$2"; }
r() { echo "== $*" | tee -a $L/summary; }
same() { cmp packages/cli/src/main $L/try.rel && echo "CMP ok: $1" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "CMP FAIL: $1" | tee -a $L/summary; }
{
r "the new compiler's binary, held to itself"
cold; $B build packages/cli --release > $L/base.rel.log 2>&1; echo "base rel exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; settle
cold; $B build packages/cli > $L/base.dev.log 2>&1; echo "base dev exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; settle
cold; $T build packages/cli --release > $L/try.rel.log 2>&1; echo "try rel exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; settle; cp packages/cli/src/main $L/try.rel
cold; AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_OFF=1 $T build packages/cli --release > $L/try.rel.off.log 2>&1; settle; same "ahead off, cold"
cold; $T build packages/cli > $L/try.dev.log 2>&1; echo "try dev exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary
$T build packages/cli --release > $L/try.rel.afterdev.log 2>&1; settle; same "ahead on, after dev"
for n in 1 2 3; do cold; AVRA_WORK_AHEAD_CORES=$n $T build packages/cli --release > $L/try.rel.c$n.log 2>&1; settle; same "$n core(s), cold"; done
cold; AVRA_WAVE_ALONE=1 $T build packages/cli --release > $L/try.rel.alone.log 2>&1; settle; same "wave alone, cold"
r "findings"
for k in rel dev; do findings $L/base.$k.log $L/base.$k.f; findings $L/try.$k.log $L/try.$k.f; cmp $L/base.$k.f $L/try.$k.f && echo "findings $k identical ($(wc -l < $L/try.$k.f) lines)" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "FINDINGS DIFFER $k" | tee -a $L/summary; done
findings $L/try.rel.off.log $L/try.rel.off.f; cmp $L/base.rel.f $L/try.rel.off.f && echo "findings rel off identical" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "FINDINGS DIFFER rel off" | tee -a $L/summary
r "fixed point"
cp $L/try.rel build/cli1; cold; build/cli1 build packages/cli --release > $L/cli1.rel.log 2>&1; echo "cli1 builds the cli: exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; settle
cmp packages/cli/src/main $L/try.rel && echo "FIXED POINT ok: the cli built by the cli the new compiler built is that cli" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "FIXED POINT FAIL" | tee -a $L/summary
findings $L/cli1.rel.log $L/cli1.rel.f; cmp $L/base.rel.f $L/cli1.rel.f && echo "findings by cli1 identical" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "FINDINGS DIFFER by cli1" | tee -a $L/summary
r "the dev-built compiler builds the release cli"
cold; $T build packages/cli > $L/dev-for-cli0.log 2>&1; settle; cp packages/cli/src/main build/cli0; find /tmp/cli0layers -delete 2>/dev/null; cp -r packages/cli/.avra-cache/tapes-build/layers /tmp/cli0layers
cold; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/cli0layers/overlay:$(ls -d /tmp/cli0layers/world-*) build/cli0 build packages/cli --release > $L/cli0.rel.log 2>&1; echo "dev-built cli builds the release cli: exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; settle
cmp packages/cli/src/main $L/try.rel && echo "CMP ok: the release cli the dev-built cli made is the try compiler's" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "CMP FAIL: dev-built cli's release cli" | tee -a $L/summary
findings $L/cli0.rel.log $L/cli0.rel.f; cmp $L/base.rel.f $L/cli0.rel.f && echo "findings by the dev-built cli identical" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "FINDINGS DIFFER by the dev-built cli" | tee -a $L/summary
r "gen2 checks std-avrac cold"
cold; build/cli1 check packages/std-avrac > $L/gen2-check.log 2>&1; echo "release gen2 check std-avrac: exit $?, language.defect $(grep -ac 'language.defect' $L/gen2-check.log)" | tee -a $L/summary
cold; LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/tmp/cli0layers/overlay:$(ls -d /tmp/cli0layers/world-*) build/cli0 check packages/std-avrac > $L/gen2-dev-check.log 2>&1; echo "dev gen2 check std-avrac: exit $?, language.defect $(grep -ac 'language.defect' $L/gen2-dev-check.log)" | tee -a $L/summary
r "the self-built compiler under the RC guard"
find /tmp/guard-one -delete 2>/dev/null; mkdir -p /tmp/guard-one; cp packages/std-avrac/src/features/fns/tests/early_return/early_return.av /tmp/guard-one/
AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 build/cli1 build /tmp/guard-one/early_return.av > $L/guard-one.log 2>&1; echo "guarded cli1 builds a program: exit $? $(grep -aci 'released twice\|double\|guard' $L/guard-one.log) guard lines" | tee -a $L/summary
(cd /tmp/guard-one && AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 ./early_return > out 2>&1; echo "its run under the guard: exit $?"; diff -q out /work/avra/packages/std-avrac/src/features/fns/tests/early_return/early_return.expected && echo "output as expected") | tee -a $L/summary
r "every emitted fn verified"
cold; AVRA_VERIFY_LLVM=1 $T build packages/cli > $L/verified.log 2>&1; echo "verified dev build exit $? ($(grep -ac 'verification failed' $L/verified.log) failures)" | tee -a $L/summary; settle
r "guarded program tests (fns, defers, loops, results, nullable)"
sh /work/lane/guarded.sh $T $L/guarded-try.txt; sh /work/lane/guarded.sh $B $L/guarded-base.txt
echo "try: $(awk '{print $2}' $L/guarded-try.txt | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ') | base: $(awk '{print $2}' $L/guarded-base.txt | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')" | tee -a $L/summary
diff <(awk '{print $1, $2}' $L/guarded-base.txt) <(awk '{print $1, $2}' $L/guarded-try.txt) > /dev/null && echo "guarded verdicts identical" | tee -a $L/summary || echo "GUARDED VERDICTS DIFFER" | tee -a $L/summary
r "suites and witnesses"
AVRA_STORE_KEPT_HERE=1 $T test packages/std-program > $L/std-program.log 2>&1; echo "std-program test exit $?: $(grep -a 'tests passed' $L/std-program.log | tail -1)" | tee -a $L/summary
sh tools/witness_program_runs.sh build/avra-try > $L/runs.log 2>&1; echo "witness_program_runs exit $?" | tee -a $L/summary; tail -3 $L/runs.log | tee -a $L/summary
AHEAD_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/ahead_edit_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
HEIR_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/heir_save_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
HELD_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/held_store_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
SHARE_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/share_merge_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
WAVE_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/wave_share_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
BESIDE_ATTACK_AVRA=$T sh tools/beside_attack.sh 2>&1 | tail -2 | tee -a $L/summary
r "a store an older compiler left, read by this one"
if [ -x "$OLD" ]; then
  cold; $OLD build packages/cli > $L/old-store.log 2>&1; settle; echo "old-format packs: $(ls packages/cli/.avra-cache/tapes/*.pack | while read f; do tail -c 8 $f; echo; done | sort | uniq -c | tr '\n' ' ')" | tee -a $L/summary

# HANDOFF — avra-lane-parallel-main

## Lane and scope
`avra-lane-parallel-main`: program-layer query engine and pack performance, the compiler's own RC traffic
(architecture item #10), and urgent measurements for the lead. Reports to the lead through the bridge. Rules:
commit on own branch, push nowhere, no `rm` (use `find -delete`), no stash, no `reset --hard`, no `--no-verify`,
fmt touched `.av` files, one heavy build at a time, idioms check with 0 NEW sites.

## Base
batch 53 = `d5062c32` (its prerequisite is `d750dfa7`). The bundle `/work/handoff/lane.bundle` holds 3 branches,
cut against `^d5062c32`.

## Commits ahead of d5062c32

### Branch `avra-lane-parallel-main` (for batch 54)
- `751ef11d` A value of parts is held and passed as its leaves; a level-0 object answers one through a lent pointer
  (leaf scalars; gate.sh conflict resolved as a union adding `level_mix_attack`)
- `a391030b` Every pack keeps its tables' slots: a lookup probes, never searches (pack hash index, seal `avrapak7`;
  `avrapak6` still read)
- `0f078f1c` tools/bodies_wave.sh: the bodies wave's table, by query family on the engine's clock

### Branch `lent-answers` (on top of 0f078f1c)
- `56654d45` WIP: lent answers. **Never compiled yet.**

### Branch `rc-kinds` (on top of 0f078f1c)
- `76d99c36` WIP: census by kind (`AVRA_RC_KINDS`). A measurement instrument; not meant to land as is.

## In flight
1. **Proof R53 of the batch-54 branch** (`OLD=$PWD/build/avra-base bash /work/lane/proofR.sh R53` in `/work/avra`).
   Summary: `/work/lane/proof-R53/summary`, copied to `notes/proof-R53-summary.txt`.
   - Passed so far: binary held to itself (ahead off, after dev, 1/2/3 cores); findings; fixed point;
     the dev-built cli; gen2; the verified build; guarded verdicts identical to base (90 ok, 13 BUILD-FAIL, 2 DIFF on both).
   - Was in "suites and witnesses" when the session ended.
   - The batch-54 bundle was NOT sent yet. To send it: finish or rerun the proof, then
     `git bundle create /work/avra-lane-parallel-main.bundle avra-lane-parallel-main ^d5062c32` and post the path.
2. **#10, lent answers (step 4)**: design posted and APPROVED. The code is written in commit `56654d45`, never built.
   - Where the mark lives: `SeatMark.lent` (core/types.av; not part of type identity / `mark_word`).
     It is inferred per lowered instance in `item_lowered.av` (`lendable_seats`, `in_own_impl`) from the IR by
     `memory.av` `lent_seats`/`answer_chain`. Every answer must be a field/index/arm projection of an eligible
     seat, every chain register `.Boxed` with no cell, and no chain register written in place.
   - How it travels: `LoweredFn.lent` → `BodySeen.lent` → `seat_marks()` in item_program.av.
   - Caller side: `lent_reads` rewrites `Call(dst)` into `Call(tmp)` + `CallRt(dst, "avra_lent_view", [src, tmp])`,
     one per lent seat, chained. The new rows are in runtime_api.av, with the C bodies in avra_hot.c and the
     interp host `RtHost.LentView`. Twin-or-view is decided by the existing machinery, plus two rules:
     - `lent_exposed`: a source reaching a cell takes the owned twin;
     - `held_over`: releases of views held across the call wait until after the lent views.
   - Callee side: `lent_answer` chain registers take no owned twin, no yield retain, no adoption, no merge
     management, and no early-answer retain.
   - Soundness (soundness.av): `lent_chain` treats a verified chain as immortal; `read_as_lent` means a lent call's
     tmp is not owning; `unlent_reads` is a defect for a view read over a seat the callee doesn't lend.
   - Attack test: `features/fns/tests/lent_answers/` (`.expected` reasoned by hand). It covers overwritten,
     rebound, consumed, yielded, stored in a cell and in a list, temporaries, two seats, early returns, a `mut` seat
     emptying the source, the arena methods, recursion, dyn, a fn value, and the generic `head<string>`/`head<int>`.

## Next 3 items, in order
1. Build `lent-answers` (`AVRA_FRAME_POINTERS=1 make try` in a worktree; a compiler copied into the tree's `build/`).
   Fix compile errors. Then:
   - run lent_answers under `avra test` (eval == native) and under `AVRA_RC_GUARD=1`;
   - run `/work/lane/guarded.sh`;
   - run `AVRA_SOUND_CHECK=1` on a cli build;
   - add the lead's extra attacks if not covered (both-lent arms: done as `either`; generic per instance: done as
     `head`, which could be strengthened);
   - measure the cut with the rc-kinds census;
   - post, then run the full proof (`proofR.sh`).
2. Finish proof R53 and send the batch-54 bundle (above).
3. #10 step (3): move at last use, extended. Expected about 0.16 G retains: outer-scope owned 0.03, params 0.12
   (needs consumed marks), dying pack parts 0.04. After that, reuse-in-place for record rebuilds (not yet measured).

## Open rulings and asks
- Lead approved (4) and then (3). Conditions on (4):
  - the mark is inferred, never written by the user;
  - it is part of the signature facts;
  - the GUARD attack suite, eval == native, and soundness proof all pass.
- Two extra attacks were asked: arms projecting different seats, and a generic whose instances differ.
- One deviation from the posted design, to tell the lead: the mark is inferred from the lowered IR per instance,
  not the AST. That makes it exact per generic fill and consistent with the memory pass.
- Bisect results were posted. The lead routed both law_findings regressions to resolve-2: fc14b4b6 is fixed by c0493354;
  3d48160f's generator forcing is still open.

## #10 numbers (cold cli build, ONE process via `taskset -c 0`)
- Retains 3.40 G and releases 4.65 G in total. By kind (`notes/census-kinds1.out`, `census-kinds2.raw`, `census-kinds3.raw`;
  read them with `python3 notes/kinds.py <raw>`):
  - owned reads 1.33 G real: yielded 0.76, held across a call/bracket 0.57, into a cell 0.28, answered 0.10;
  - consuming seats 0.91 (a borrowed view 0.50, read again after 0.29, a param 0.11);
  - cell stores 0.24; loads outliving the cell 0.20; yields 0.19; packs 0.14;
  - releases: reclaim cascades 1.38, cells 0.20.

## Trip wires
- **Disk allowance**: about 39 GB. Delete `packages/cli/.avra-cache` in old worktrees; `/work/avra-fp` and
  `/work/avra-b` (bisect trees) are deletable.
- **The census sums RSS across forks**. Run it as
  `taskset -c 0 env CENSUS_CAP_MB=14000 CENSUS_BUILDER=<builder> sh tools/census.sh build packages/cli`.
  The census only reports the parent process, so forks lose counts.
- **Kinds census builder**: `notes/kb.sh` sets `AVRA_RC_KINDS=1` for the builder only.
- **`make try` in a worktree** can leave `build/llvm_wrapper.o`, `ffi.o` and `std_*.o` missing. Rebuild them with
  `make build/llvm_wrapper.o build/ffi.o build/std_io.o build/std_io_watch.o build/std_net.o build/std_process.o build/std_time.o`.
- **"No std stands beside this compiler"**: run compilers from inside a tree's `build/`.
- **Kept binaries in `/work/avra/build`**: `avra-try` (the batch-54 branch) and `avra-base` (batch 53).
  The bisect compilers are in `/work/bisect/`.
- **`LLVM_PREFIX=/usr/lib/llvm-22`**; `. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh`.
- **Worktrees**: `/work/avra-lent` (lent-answers) and `/work/avra-kinds` (rc-kinds).

  one built from a different TYPE SHAPE costs an afternoon, so a lane
  that bootstraps through any shape it will revert clears `.avra-cache`
  before the run whose ANSWER it reads.

  binary aside (`cp build/avra build/avra.pre`), build the product

  product, gate. The product refuses the old form, so a broken
  product leaves no compiler — the saved copy is the way back. And
  the script must never cross a SYMLINK into another tree

  existing one is a defect in the ASSEMBLED grammar — "branches 1 and

  COMPILER'S OWN SOURCE DECLARES CANNOT BE GATED IN THE COMMIT THAT
  ADDS IT. A declaration naming an `rt_sigs` row is legal only to a
  compiler that ALREADY CARRIES the row — `crossing_law` exempts a
  row's name by asking its own `rt_sigs()` — so a tree that adds the
  row and declares it in the same breath is refused by every compiler
  that could build it: the standing binary, the committed seed, and
  therefore `seed-check` and `make bootstrap` alike. THE BRANCH CANNOT
  GATE BY CONSTRUCTION, and the first buildable point is a tree
  carrying BOTH the row and a seed that knows it.

  `Unhosted` — which is TRUE, since the evaluator has no arm yet —
  with its C body and whatever keeper table names it, is ONE commit,
  marked with a `Rung: <why>` trailer; the declaration, the `RtHost`
  variant and its arm, and the callers are the next. CI builds the tree
  at each mark with the product of the one before it (tools/ladder.sh,
  the one definition CI and a Sprite share), never with a compiler that
  cannot read it, and HEAD last, twice, as for any tree; the whole
  ladder is capped at fifteen minutes and costs about one generation
  per rung. A rung's product is cached per PR, so a re-push that leaves
  the marked commits alone pays only HEAD. The squash merge drops the
  rung trees, so main's own run reads `(#N)` from the title and replays
  the ladder from `refs/pull/N/head`, which GitHub keeps. `seed-check`

  build a tree whose reader needs the row it lacks, by construction —
  and the seed refresh is owed after the landing, not before it. A
  tree whose compiler failed to build a rung says which rung and shows
  its log: the way out is a rung boundary one commit earlier, never a
  bypass. Before the ladder this took two landings with a seed refresh
  between them; the law that survives is the first sentence of this
  entry: no single TREE can be gated by a compiler that lacks its row,
  only a chain of trees can.
  AND A ROW WHOSE SEAT TAKES A BOX HAS THREE RUNGS: the row, its arm,
  its declaration. `crossing_law` exempts a row only when it is ARMED
  — an arm is what materialises the aggregate — so a compiler that
  knows a row `Unhosted` refuses a box at its seat exactly as one that
  has never heard of it. Probed at `590f8e3`, the rows known and
  `Unhosted`: `extern fn avra_gate_new() -> List<int>` is
  `type.host_seat` "the answer of `avra_gate_new` wears `List<int>`,
  which cannot cross to C", while the same row declared `-> ptr`, and
  every word seat, checks clean. So the arm lands with word and `ptr`
  seats alone — the evaluator's own source declares the row it arms,
  and a box there would need the armed compiler to build the arm — the
  seed is refreshed, and only then does a declaration spell the box.
  A PLACEHOLDER ARM IS NOT NEEDED AND SHOULD NOT BE WRITTEN. `Unhosted`
  already says what is true and already has its arm; inventing a
  temporary variant to delete next week is a comment about a point in
  time wearing code's clothes.
- A RECORD-LITERAL RESOLUTION IS A UNION OF FIELD LISTS, never either
  side's line. A merge that resolves a struct/record literal by taking
  ONE side wholesale silently deletes a field the other side added,
  and the compiler's F2010 ("every declared field appears exactly
  once") is what catches the loss. A record literal is the one place in
  a conflict where `--theirs` must never be taken whole: every other
  shape can be read and picked, but a literal's field list is merged.
  (Paid assembling phase D onto the milestone: `NodeStore`'s literal
  took the cursor's line and dropped main's `grammars:` field.)
- THE RECEIPT FOR A SLICE THAT REMOVES A RUNTIME SYMBOL IS `make
  bootstrap` GREEN, NEVER `make avra` GREEN. `make avra` builds the
  cli with the STANDING binary and copies the result; it never
  touches `bootstrap/seed.ll`, which is a COMMITTED artifact naming
  every runtime symbol it needs, the `avra_io_` names among them. So

  that SURVIVED into package C; one deleted by design exists nowhere

content.content:
## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
  the category.
- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.

## Dogfooding is design

The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.

## Rules
## The subset today

What our compiler REFUSES that the language will want. THE SECTION IS
EXECUTABLE: every refusal below is a case in
`packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/subset/` pinning its kind, its
words and its message count, and every fact under "Runtime facts" is a
case that runs the program. An entry the compiler starts accepting
turns its case red — delete the case and its line together. A new entry
lands WITH its case; a line without one says so. Each entry is a
sugar-backlog candidate, not a trap to write around: write the form the
compiler's help names, and when a site wants the missing form, add the
ask to the ROADMAP's sugar backlog naming the site. Laws that SPEAK are
not listed — reserved words (F3002), a mutating method on a non-`mut`
binding (F2034), a lambda assigning to a capture (F3005), a fn body
reading a top-level `let` (F3020), an extra method inside an `impl
Trait for` (F2032), an exported name declared twice across a module's
files (F3017), a wrong payload count (F2015), a `DeclId` in a `StmtId`
seat (F2000): the compiler's help is the note.

Syntax the grammar lacks:
- An import is spelled with DOTS: `use @std.io.{read_text}`; `use @std/io.{…}` is "expected `.`" at the slash (prose says `@std/io`, the `use` line never does).
- Or-patterns spell `or`, in patterns only; `|` is "expected `}` to close the `match`", and `or`/`and` as booleans are "expected BREAK" — the operators are `&&`, `||`, `!`.
- `[i for (i, m) in xs.enumerate()]` — "`enumerate` pairs only under a paired `for` head"; write `[f(i, x) for i, x in xs]`.
- `int??` has no spelling ("expected `)`"/"expected `=`" at the first `?`) though a generic reaches `string??`.
- A bare `table { … }` reads as a struct literal ("no `type table` is declared"); write `table<Row> { id | name … }` with a pipe header.
- A record literal as a component instance's head stands in parentheses (`tally (Span { n: 2 }) { extra: 3 }`); bare, the brace opens the block — pinned by features/components/tests/components_head_test.av, not by this section.
- A semicolon between statements is "unexpected character `;`"; a one-line body is `{ a }`.
- A field's mark on its own line inside a type literal is "expected `}` while parsing `stmt`"; write it on the field's line (`{ @local at: int }`).
- `if let v? = e { … }` takes an `else`: without one it is "expected BREAK" at the `let`; a guard is `let v? = e else { … }`, and a present-only test is `if e != null { … }`.
- A range takes methods (`any`, `find`, `map`, `all`) but has no `.length`.
- A `once fn` takes no type parameters ("expected `(`"), no arguments, and answers a managed value ("`once fn seed` answers `int`, which the runtime cannot keep").
- A trailing block in a head (`if f(a) { x -> x } { … }`) is "expected BREAK"; parenthesise the call. `a?.m { … }` and `(f(a)) { … }` take no trailing block either — not pinned.
- A seat default lands on `fn`, `mut fn`, `static fn` and a trait's `fn` (whose default every impl takes) only: `extern fn` and a lambda refuse it ("expected `)`", "expected `)` to close the group"); a named argument skips a defaulted seat; a default reads no sibling param; a fn value of a defaulted fn wears every seat.
- A generic fn as a value: pinned `ident<int>` is "expected BREAK"; bare is "a generic fn is not a value — no single signature to wear".
- Instantiation is a statement: as a fn's tail it answers `void` — bind, then return the name; a component block is `key: value` ("declares no `List` field, so its block holds settings only") — not pinned.
- A shell `${VAR}` in a string is Avra's interpolation ("`HOME` is not defined", or silently the binding's value); write `$VAR`.
- `_` is a parameter name nowhere ("`_` is a keyword"); an unread seat is `_q`, and `let _ = f()` is the binding spelling.
- A map's keys are strings only ("a map's keys are strings, not `int`").
- `xs ++ ys` is "expected BREAK"; `xs.concat(ys)` or `[..xs, ..ys]`.
- `List` has `all`, not `every`.
- A spread's refusals are laws, not pending sugar (`..` is one spelling in a record literal, list, map, variadic seat, call's named seats and pattern): a record spreads only under its type's name (`{ ..a, x: 3 }` is a map: "`..` in a map spreads a map, found `P`"); a record pattern's `..` discards, so `P { x, ..rest }` is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; a list spreads only into its own element type; `f(..xs)` into fixed seats is "`..` spreads into a seat that takes the rest of the arguments"; `is` over a list or record pattern binds only under `if` (`type.is_bind`) and a refutable destructuring `let` needs its `else` (`type.let_pattern`).
- A match arm on the brace's line needs a trailing comma before the next arm ("expected `}` to close the `match`", reported at the second arm); each arm on its own line parses.
- A present-bind arm (`v? -> …`) after a comma-ended arm, or itself ending in a comma, is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; separate such arms by line.
- An empty block as a match arm is an empty map: "a `match`'s arms disagree: `{}` vs the first arm's `void`".
- A `\u` escape is not one: `"\u0041"` keeps its six characters, as do `\0` and `\u{…}` (see Runtime facts); spell a code point with `@std/text`'s `from_codepoint(65533)` and a NUL with `from_codepoint(0)` (sugar backlog: `\u{…}` escapes).
- A bare name in a pattern is a const's or a binder's by its binding, never its spelling: `type.const_pattern` warns when a match ENDS on a const's name and `type.unreachable_arm` when a binder precedes a literal arm (the const-comparison law itself is not pinned here; features/enums/tests/const_pat_template is).
- A match arm whose body is a bare statement (`.Bad(t) -> fail E.Bad(t),`) fails the whole file ("expected `}` to close the `match`"); brace it.
- `get(i)?.name` and `shell(line)?.run()` lex as `?.` ("`?.` reaches into a nullable, this is `Result<…>`"); write `(get(i)?).name`.
- `export let` is "`export` marks a fn, type, enum or trait — not this statement"; `export const` lands.
- `Result<void, E>` is "a `Result` side cannot hold `void` yet"; a writing verb answers what it wrote.
- A `mut` seat cannot be assigned whole, by design: "a seat is written along a path, never replaced whole" — use a `Cell<T>`, a path write, or answer the new value.
- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".

Wants the typer does not carry yet:
- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
- A generic struct literal's field seat unifies instead of planting a want: an unpinned `mk()` there is "`N` is not pinned by the arguments".
- A lambda in a field or argument seat does not read the seat's answer ("`.Ok` needs a known enum"); a typed `let` does, and a named fn works everywhere.
- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.
- A bound lands on a free fn's and a component's parameters only: `type T<K: Tr, V>` and `impl T<K: Tr, V>` are "expected `=`"/"expected `{`", a generic method is "generic methods are recorded, not landed"; a generic container keyed by a typed id keys by the slot (core's `SideTable`).
- Variant arms or `is` over a nullable enum are "`match` chooses over an enum, found `K?`" / "`is` asks an enum for its variant, found `K?`"; unwrap first.
- A bound method as a value (`xs.any(self.rides)`) is read as a property ("no field `rides` on `S`"); write `(k) -> self.rides(k)`.
- `it` through a self-method wrapper (`xs.any(self.rides(it))`) is "`it` has no element here"; `it` binds to the nearest call, and a pipe stage is such a call.
- `[1, 2].join(",")` is "`join` reads a list of text, this one holds `int`"; map to text first.
- `==`, `contains`/`index_of` and a literal pattern compare a scalar, text, a tagged enum, or a one-field record; two fields is "`==` compares by value — …", and an enum carrying a payload is refused too (help: match on it).
- A named type is opaque at a seat and transparent at a read: a `Rows` seat refuses a computed `List<int>` ("wants `Rows`, found `List<int>`") and takes a literal.
- `r catch null` answers the ok side, so `let x? = r catch null else { … }` is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side: `D`, this is `null`" (and "`x?` asks a nullable"); a `Result` read as absence is a `match` (`.Ok(d) -> d, .Err(_) -> null`).

Methods the runtime lacks:
- `List.reverse()` / `sort()` are "calls a method, and `List<int>` has none"; core's `reversed` is the helper.
- `m["k"]` on a map is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Map<string, int>`"; `.get(k)` answers `T?`.
- `b[0]` on `Bytes` is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Bytes`"; `b.at(i)` reads an octet and traps past the end. `[104, 105].bytes()` answers `Bytes?` ("declares `Bytes`, this is `Bytes?`"), and `.at` on it is refused.

Runtime facts, ours to ratify:
- `split` drops a trailing empty segment and keeps a leading one (`".a"` two, `"a."` one, `""` none).
- `"\u0041".length` is 6, `"ab\0cd".length` is 6 and `"\u{1F600}".length` is 9 — no `\u` or `\0` is an escape.
- A 50000-deep recursion runs in `avra run`; a runaway traps at 100000 nested calls — the trap is not pinned.
- Not gate-pinned: a string's `.length` is a header load; a NUL is an ordinary character in every text verb (`from_codepoint(0)` mints one; `==`, `contains`, `starts_with` walk the header); `parse_int` takes exactly `-`? digits and answers the smallest int whole; `Bytes` text readers (`text()`, `text_prefix()`, `text_lossy()`). Each wants a case.

## How work lands

The single source for the landing path, Sprites, the watcher and the
CI gates is `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`; the section below is the
doctrine it expands.

- ALL WORK MOVES THROUGH SEVEN COMMANDS, and nothing else touches main:

      sh tools/work new <name>   # a worktree ../avra-<name> off main, and its Sprite
      sh tools/work run <cmd>    # run it on a GitHub runner (--sprite: the lane's Sprite), its exit status
      sh tools/work test         # what this branch touches, on this lane's Sprite
      sh tools/work land         # push, PR, arm auto-merge — no Sprite involved
      sh tools/work status       # PRs and their merge state; each lane and its Sprite
      sh tools/work sprites      # every Sprite at a glance; `--fix [name]` repairs
      sh tools/work unbind       # end this lane's run, free its Sprite, keep the worktree
      sh tools/work done --remove-worktree   # remove this lane too: ONLY with the owner's say-so

  Main lives on GitHub (avra-lang/avra): squash merges, linear history,
  no direct pushes. It requires the `test` check AND that a branch be up
  to date with it, and auto-merge lands a green, current PR by itself,
  one at a time. A local main
  only follows `origin/main` (the reference-transaction hook refuses any
  other update; a deliberate repair sets `AVRA_MAIN_OVERRIDE="<reason>"`).
- THE PR IS THE TRAIN, AND THERE IS NO MERGE QUEUE (dropped 2026-10-11:
  its only real value was testing `main` plus every PR ahead, which
  "require up to date" gives back for free one PR at a time, while the
  queue cost trains that tested many PRs at once — one red suite killed
  them all — HEADGREEN batching and a rebase treadmill). A PR's `test`
  check IS the gate, on the PR's own tree (`.github/workflows/
  checks.yml`): fmt on its changed `.av`, idioms and suites over the
  packages it TOUCHES, the compiler-dependent keepers, the seed check and
  the affected packages' suites; a PR that touches no `.av`, no package
  and no compiler source builds nothing. Before it builds anything it
  runs the keepers that need NO COMPILER (`make keepers-static`, half a
  minute), so a refusal one of them speaks stops on the PR. Because the
  branch must be up to date, the tree it tests already holds `main`, so a
  cross-PR interaction (two individually-green PRs
  colliding on a latent bug) is caught on the later PR's own run. THE
  COMPILER IS CACHED BY
  ITS OWN SOURCE (`tools/compiler_paths.sh`): a tree whose compiler is
  main's takes main's binary; otherwise the newest cached binary builds
  the tree twice (the generation law), and one too old to read it — new
  syntax, a new refusal about its own source — fails that build and the
  tree BOOTSTRAPS from the committed seed. Main's own push run caches
  the compiler every run starts from.
- A LANE ITERATES WITH `make try`, NEVER `make avra`: it builds the
  compiler with the STANDING `build/avra` into `build/avra-try` and never
  replaces the builder, so its store stays warm (a leaf edit, ~4 s held
  464/466) and `./avra-try <cmd>` probes the change. `make avra` is for
  a change the compiler must READ to build itself — codegen, the front
  end, a refusal about its own source — and before landing.
- A PRE-COMMIT HOOK refuses staged `.av` that is not canonical; the fix
  it prints is `build/avra fmt --write <files>`. Never `--no-verify`.
- HEAVY RUNS GO ON SPRITES, ONE SPRITE A LANE: `sh tools/work run <cmd>`
  from inside the worktree. `work new` binds a free Sprite (`work bind`
  for a worktree that has none, `work unbind` frees it), and the lane's
  tree and compiler stay warm there between runs. Bootstraps, whole
  suites and censuses run there; the Mac keeps quick targeted checks and
  anything macOS-only. ONE RUN PER SPRITE, EVERY STEP BOUNDED: `run`
  answers the command's status, or 76 (busy), 70 (the compiler does not
  build), 124/125 (a bound; `--for <minutes>` raises the command's), 137
  (out of memory), 75 (the Sprite did not answer), 74 (the provider did
  not answer) — and a failure's last line begins with the one of three
  that failed: SPRITE, CONNECTION or COMMAND. A RUN BELONGS TO THE
  SPRITE, NOT TO THE CONNECTION: a supervisor there keeps its output and
  status and holds the Sprite awake while it lives, `run` only follows
  it, and a dropped connection is followed again from the byte it stood
  at — so Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the
  client being killed never does (it says so, and the next `run` answers
  76 until `work attach` has followed it out); a run is as long as its
  `--for` says, and the Sprite ends it at its bound whoever is
  watching (`work attach` follows again, `work stop` ends it, `work
  done` ends it with the lane). `sh tools/work sprites` shows all of
  them in seconds.
  A RUN ANSWERS ABOUT THIS WORKTREE OR NOT AT ALL: rsync carries files
  to the Sprite, a file the worktree no longer has is removed there by
  name, and the Sprite's manifest (every path and its hash) must equal
  the worktree's before anything starts — else `SPRITE — sync:` and 75.
  What a run wrote is left: `build/`, `.avra-cache`, anything git ignores.
  WHAT ENDS A RUN EARLY IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: a twenty-minute exec holds,
  chatty or silent, and thirty-two spinning processes leave a Sprite
  answering in a second — but a Sprite says 16 GB and a balloon holds
  half, more while it idles (3.3 to 7.3 GB were free to a run), there is
  no swap, and under about 250 MB the whole machine answers nobody for
  minutes. The Sprite's keeper ends a run at 600 MB (137), and every run
  says what it had to start with. A SPRITE WITH NO SESSION AND NO HOLD
  IS SUSPENDED WITHIN SECONDS, MID-WRITE IF NEED BE, which is why
  nothing runs there detached without the hold; one silent for minutes
  has lost its filesystem and is destroyed and created again
  (provisioning is `run`'s first step, from `.github/ci/packages.txt`).
  WHAT HOLDS A SPRITE AWAKE WITH NOBODY ATTACHED IS ITS TASKS API AND
  NOTHING ELSE WE TRIED, measured over 400 s without contact: a task
  refreshed each minute, no gap; a detached TTY session that prints, no
  gap; a running service, a 372 s gap; outbound traffic, frozen at once;
  an exec from outside every 20 s, one tick each. And a task's name is
  lowercase letters, digits and dashes or the Sprite answers 400 — a
  run is named after the machine that began it, capitals and all, so the
  hold is asked under a name made to fit and ITS ANSWER IS READ. A run
  that stood still says for how long in its own output, and `work
  sprites` shows it beside how long the run has been quiet.
- A BRANCH IS REBASED ONTO `origin/main` ONLY, never onto another
  unlanded branch: that lands the other branch's work unverified. A
  branch built on a stale local main moves with `git rebase --onto
  origin/main main <branch>`, which carries only its own commits.
- A PID IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS KILLED. A recorded pid is reused once
  its process exits; read `ps -o command= -p <pid>` first.
- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
  correct work.
- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

## Working discipline

- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
  lane's own PR was failing the train.)

- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
  `tools/work land`
  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.
- A GEN-N VS GEN-N+1 DIVERGENCE IS FOUND BY TRACING, NEVER GUESSED.
  `AVRA_QTRACE=1` prints one stderr line per query-kernel event —
  every `Memo.ask` (family, arg, reuse/compute/cycle) and
  `Memo.settle` (family, arg, fingerprint) in @std/relation's
  engine/answers.av, every
  `Binder.declare` (name, file) in features/namespace.av, every
  failed `named_type` lookup in compiler/typing/declare.av, every
  file a check PARSES (`Q parse <path>`, compiler/program.av), every
  ATTEMPT a derivation makes (`Q attempt <turn> hold … reading <n>`,
  compiler/derive.av) — behind
  `avra_qtrace` (runtime/avra_runtime.c), inert without the flag.
  Run both binaries on the SAME input with `AVRA_QTRACE=1`, confirm
  each is deterministic against itself (diff two runs of the same
  binary — must be empty), then diff the two traces: the FIRST
  differing line names the query whose answer diverged first. Add a
  probe at the divergent query's own site the same way — one

- WHICH COPY FORKED IS ANSWERED BY A CLONE LOG, NEVER BY READING THE

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
  want)`, `cx.open_region(c)`, `ws.sig(d)` — 320 verbs, one sweep);
  style.free_state_verb refuses a new free verb in the pass's own files. A PASS ENTRY
  POINT (`lower(a: Analysis)`, `memory(l: Lowered)`) keeps the one
  standard signature and is not a verb.
- A long fn splits at its PHASE boundaries into named helpers, each
  with a one-line contract (`match_seq` matches, `built` builds —
  grammar/executor.av; `window` frames, `severity_word` branches —
  diagnostics/render.av). If a fn needs a paragraph comment
  mid-body, that paragraph is a helper's name.
- A LAW never assembles PROSE: every refusal is a NAMED VOICE fn
  (its whole body the one `spoken`/`emit`), in a voices section at
  the file's tail or shared where features share words. Rule
  bodies read as guard + verb (rule.compiler.refusal_assembled;
  enums/check.av is the exemplar).
  AND A VOICE STATES THE LAW, NOT THE SYMPTOM. "a pointer's only
  constant is null" is the rule; "both engines read it as null" was
  the observation that happened to hold the day it was written. A
  symptom-worded refusal goes STALE the moment the mechanism moves,
  and until then it reads as a workaround for a quirk rather than a
  rule to obey — so it teaches the reader to look for the quirk. The
  law's wording outlives its own implementation, which is what makes
  it worth pinning in the golden (lower.av's pointer-constant guard).
- A BUILDER'S WORDS ARE ITS CLAIM. A builder's refusal is carried
  WHOLE into its diagnostic (grammar/executor.av's build phase:
  `cause: Cause.Builder, message: m`), so a message that is a LAW
  the writer broke reads as the law, and one that is a DEFECT says
  so in its own words. A blanket "builder failed:" prefix once told
  the reader the compiler had broken about every law — five of the
  seven refusals sampled at c7b5038 — while `Cause` had separated
  `Builder` from `Defect` all along: the seam was right and only the
  WORDING lied. THE GENERAL SHAPE: A PARAPHRASE OF A FLAG IS A
  SECOND COPY, and the reader believes the words — the flag is
  checked by the code, the prose by nobody. So the WORDS carry the
  CLAIM and the STRUCTURE carries the CATEGORY (`Cause.Builder`
  projects to F0102, compiler/codes.av), and the words never restate
  the category.
- A projection is ONE match: nested patterns
  (`.Node(.NAlt(a)) -> a, _ -> null`), never an unwrap ladder.
- The third copy of a shape names the concept: shared walks and
  registries get ONE definition (`post_order`, `file_command`) and
  the copies die. Two copies may wait; three never do.

## Dogfooding is design

The compiler is Avra's first user. When its code WANTS a construct
the language lacks — a sugar, a projection, a rule — add the ask to
the ROADMAP's sugar backlog, naming the wanting site, as part of the
change that hit it. Request your own features: the backlog feeds the
spec. The same discipline runs one level down: a PATTERN discovered
while writing (a beautiful form, a smell, a licensed exception) is
an IDIOM — it lands in DOGFOODING.md's registry at discovery, and
the greppable ones become `rule` declarations `avra check` finds
directly (compiler/idioms.av, or a feature's own idioms.av). The
registry is the idiom engine's spec, written by dogfooding.

## Rules
## The subset today

What our compiler REFUSES that the language will want. THE SECTION IS
EXECUTABLE: every refusal below is a case in
`packages/std-avrac/src/compiler/tests/subset/` pinning its kind, its
words and its message count, and every fact under "Runtime facts" is a
case that runs the program. An entry the compiler starts accepting
turns its case red — delete the case and its line together. A new entry
lands WITH its case; a line without one says so. Each entry is a
sugar-backlog candidate, not a trap to write around: write the form the
compiler's help names, and when a site wants the missing form, add the
ask to the ROADMAP's sugar backlog naming the site. Laws that SPEAK are
not listed — reserved words (F3002), a mutating method on a non-`mut`
binding (F2034), a lambda assigning to a capture (F3005), a fn body
reading a top-level `let` (F3020), an extra method inside an `impl
Trait for` (F2032), an exported name declared twice across a module's
files (F3017), a wrong payload count (F2015), a `DeclId` in a `StmtId`
seat (F2000): the compiler's help is the note.

Syntax the grammar lacks:
- An import is spelled with DOTS: `use @std.io.{read_text}`; `use @std/io.{…}` is "expected `.`" at the slash (prose says `@std/io`, the `use` line never does).
- Or-patterns spell `or`, in patterns only; `|` is "expected `}` to close the `match`", and `or`/`and` as booleans are "expected BREAK" — the operators are `&&`, `||`, `!`.
- `[i for (i, m) in xs.enumerate()]` — "`enumerate` pairs only under a paired `for` head"; write `[f(i, x) for i, x in xs]`.
- `int??` has no spelling ("expected `)`"/"expected `=`" at the first `?`) though a generic reaches `string??`.
- A bare `table { … }` reads as a struct literal ("no `type table` is declared"); write `table<Row> { id | name … }` with a pipe header.
- A record literal as a component instance's head stands in parentheses (`tally (Span { n: 2 }) { extra: 3 }`); bare, the brace opens the block — pinned by features/components/tests/components_head_test.av, not by this section.
- A semicolon between statements is "unexpected character `;`"; a one-line body is `{ a }`.
- A field's mark on its own line inside a type literal is "expected `}` while parsing `stmt`"; write it on the field's line (`{ @local at: int }`).
- `if let v? = e { … }` takes an `else`: without one it is "expected BREAK" at the `let`; a guard is `let v? = e else { … }`, and a present-only test is `if e != null { … }`.
- A range takes methods (`any`, `find`, `map`, `all`) but has no `.length`.
- A `once fn` takes no type parameters ("expected `(`"), no arguments, and answers a managed value ("`once fn seed` answers `int`, which the runtime cannot keep").
- A trailing block in a head (`if f(a) { x -> x } { … }`) is "expected BREAK"; parenthesise the call. `a?.m { … }` and `(f(a)) { … }` take no trailing block either — not pinned.
- A seat default lands on `fn`, `mut fn`, `static fn` and a trait's `fn` (whose default every impl takes) only: `extern fn` and a lambda refuse it ("expected `)`", "expected `)` to close the group"); a named argument skips a defaulted seat; a default reads no sibling param; a fn value of a defaulted fn wears every seat.
- A generic fn as a value: pinned `ident<int>` is "expected BREAK"; bare is "a generic fn is not a value — no single signature to wear".
- Instantiation is a statement: as a fn's tail it answers `void` — bind, then return the name; a component block is `key: value` ("declares no `List` field, so its block holds settings only") — not pinned.
- A shell `${VAR}` in a string is Avra's interpolation ("`HOME` is not defined", or silently the binding's value); write `$VAR`.
- `_` is a parameter name nowhere ("`_` is a keyword"); an unread seat is `_q`, and `let _ = f()` is the binding spelling.
- A map's keys are strings only ("a map's keys are strings, not `int`").
- `xs ++ ys` is "expected BREAK"; `xs.concat(ys)` or `[..xs, ..ys]`.
- `List` has `all`, not `every`.
- A spread's refusals are laws, not pending sugar (`..` is one spelling in a record literal, list, map, variadic seat, call's named seats and pattern): a record spreads only under its type's name (`{ ..a, x: 3 }` is a map: "`..` in a map spreads a map, found `P`"); a record pattern's `..` discards, so `P { x, ..rest }` is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; a list spreads only into its own element type; `f(..xs)` into fixed seats is "`..` spreads into a seat that takes the rest of the arguments"; `is` over a list or record pattern binds only under `if` (`type.is_bind`) and a refutable destructuring `let` needs its `else` (`type.let_pattern`).
- A match arm on the brace's line needs a trailing comma before the next arm ("expected `}` to close the `match`", reported at the second arm); each arm on its own line parses.
- A present-bind arm (`v? -> …`) after a comma-ended arm, or itself ending in a comma, is "expected `}` to close the `match`"; separate such arms by line.
- An empty block as a match arm is an empty map: "a `match`'s arms disagree: `{}` vs the first arm's `void`".
- A `\u` escape is not one: `"\u0041"` keeps its six characters, as do `\0` and `\u{…}` (see Runtime facts); spell a code point with `@std/text`'s `from_codepoint(65533)` and a NUL with `from_codepoint(0)` (sugar backlog: `\u{…}` escapes).
- A bare name in a pattern is a const's or a binder's by its binding, never its spelling: `type.const_pattern` warns when a match ENDS on a const's name and `type.unreachable_arm` when a binder precedes a literal arm (the const-comparison law itself is not pinned here; features/enums/tests/const_pat_template is).
- A match arm whose body is a bare statement (`.Bad(t) -> fail E.Bad(t),`) fails the whole file ("expected `}` to close the `match`"); brace it.
- `get(i)?.name` and `shell(line)?.run()` lex as `?.` ("`?.` reaches into a nullable, this is `Result<…>`"); write `(get(i)?).name`.
- `export let` is "`export` marks a fn, type, enum or trait — not this statement"; `export const` lands.
- `Result<void, E>` is "a `Result` side cannot hold `void` yet"; a writing verb answers what it wrote.
- A `mut` seat cannot be assigned whole, by design: "a seat is written along a path, never replaced whole" — use a `Cell<T>`, a path write, or answer the new value.
- Two top-level consts of one name are "defined more than once"; a `let` of that name shadows from its line on, and a fn body reads the const.
- `fail` inside a `catch` arm's block is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side"; write the statement `match`.
- `[null, null]` names no type where no seat names one ("a list element takes its type from its value"); any typed sibling or seat names it.
- A keyed list (`list xs by it.id { x -> … }`) is "`list` takes no head value"; reconciliation is positional — not pinned (needs `@std/ui`).
- `derived x = …` and `query x = …` are "expected BREAK"; recompute in a `fn` or hold a `state`.
- `@model type` is "`model` is not defined"; a plain `type` until the derive exists.
- A built-in type name is no domain type: `type Task = { … }` is "`Task` is a built-in type".

Wants the typer does not carry yet:
- A declaring annotation's argument is a literal or a const naming one: `@traced("a" + "b")` is "`traced` generates declarations, so its arguments come from the source alone" — not pinned (needs a package with `@std/meta`).
- A generic struct literal's field seat unifies instead of planting a want: an unpinned `mk()` there is "`N` is not pinned by the arguments".
- A lambda in a field or argument seat does not read the seat's answer ("`.Ok` needs a known enum"); a typed `let` does, and a named fn works everywhere.
- `Traced<E>`'s `cause`/`context`/`trace` stay inherent methods permanently (a trait member's answer is fixed by its signature); the real want is a bound on a type's own parameter.
- A bound lands on a free fn's and a component's parameters only: `type T<K: Tr, V>` and `impl T<K: Tr, V>` are "expected `=`"/"expected `{`", a generic method is "generic methods are recorded, not landed"; a generic container keyed by a typed id keys by the slot (core's `SideTable`).
- Variant arms or `is` over a nullable enum are "`match` chooses over an enum, found `K?`" / "`is` asks an enum for its variant, found `K?`"; unwrap first.
- A bound method as a value (`xs.any(self.rides)`) is read as a property ("no field `rides` on `S`"); write `(k) -> self.rides(k)`.
- `it` through a self-method wrapper (`xs.any(self.rides(it))`) is "`it` has no element here"; `it` binds to the nearest call, and a pipe stage is such a call.
- `[1, 2].join(",")` is "`join` reads a list of text, this one holds `int`"; map to text first.
- `==`, `contains`/`index_of` and a literal pattern compare a scalar, text, a tagged enum, or a one-field record; two fields is "`==` compares by value — …", and an enum carrying a payload is refused too (help: match on it).
- A named type is opaque at a seat and transparent at a read: a `Rows` seat refuses a computed `List<int>` ("wants `Rows`, found `List<int>`") and takes a literal.
- `r catch null` answers the ok side, so `let x? = r catch null else { … }` is "a `catch` arm answers the ok side: `D`, this is `null`" (and "`x?` asks a nullable"); a `Result` read as absence is a `match` (`.Ok(d) -> d, .Err(_) -> null`).

Methods the runtime lacks:
- `List.reverse()` / `sort()` are "calls a method, and `List<int>` has none"; core's `reversed` is the helper.
- `m["k"]` on a map is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Map<string, int>`"; `.get(k)` answers `T?`.
- `b[0]` on `Bytes` is "`[...]` indexes a `List`, found `Bytes`"; `b.at(i)` reads an octet and traps past the end. `[104, 105].bytes()` answers `Bytes?` ("declares `Bytes`, this is `Bytes?`"), and `.at` on it is refused.

Runtime facts, ours to ratify:
- `split` drops a trailing empty segment and keeps a leading one (`".a"` two, `"a."` one, `""` none).
- `"\u0041".length` is 6, `"ab\0cd".length` is 6 and `"\u{1F600}".length` is 9 — no `\u` or `\0` is an escape.
- A 50000-deep recursion runs in `avra run`; a runaway traps at 100000 nested calls — the trap is not pinned.
- Not gate-pinned: a string's `.length` is a header load; a NUL is an ordinary character in every text verb (`from_codepoint(0)` mints one; `==`, `contains`, `starts_with` walk the header); `parse_int` takes exactly `-`? digits and answers the smallest int whole; `Bytes` text readers (`text()`, `text_prefix()`, `text_lossy()`). Each wants a case.

## How work lands

The single source for the landing path, Sprites, the watcher and the
CI gates is `docs/2026_10_11_THE_PIPELINE.md`; the section below is the
doctrine it expands.

- ALL WORK MOVES THROUGH SEVEN COMMANDS, and nothing else touches main:

      sh tools/work new <name>   # a worktree ../avra-<name> off main, and its Sprite
      sh tools/work run <cmd>    # run it on a GitHub runner (--sprite: the lane's Sprite), its exit status
      sh tools/work test         # what this branch touches, on this lane's Sprite
      sh tools/work land         # push, PR, arm auto-merge — no Sprite involved
      sh tools/work status       # PRs and their merge state; each lane and its Sprite
      sh tools/work sprites      # every Sprite at a glance; `--fix [name]` repairs
      sh tools/work unbind       # end this lane's run, free its Sprite, keep the worktree
      sh tools/work done --remove-worktree   # remove this lane too: ONLY with the owner's say-so

  Main lives on GitHub (avra-lang/avra): squash merges, linear history,
  no direct pushes. It requires the `test` check AND that a branch be up
  to date with it, and auto-merge lands a green, current PR by itself,
  one at a time. A local main
  only follows `origin/main` (the reference-transaction hook refuses any
  other update; a deliberate repair sets `AVRA_MAIN_OVERRIDE="<reason>"`).
- THE PR IS THE TRAIN, AND THERE IS NO MERGE QUEUE (dropped 2026-10-11:
  its only real value was testing `main` plus every PR ahead, which
  "require up to date" gives back for free one PR at a time, while the
  queue cost trains that tested many PRs at once — one red suite killed
  them all — HEADGREEN batching and a rebase treadmill). A PR's `test`
  check IS the gate, on the PR's own tree (`.github/workflows/
  checks.yml`): fmt on its changed `.av`, idioms and suites over the
  packages it TOUCHES, the compiler-dependent keepers, the seed check and
  the affected packages' suites; a PR that touches no `.av`, no package
  and no compiler source builds nothing. Before it builds anything it
  runs the keepers that need NO COMPILER (`make keepers-static`, half a
  minute), so a refusal one of them speaks stops on the PR. Because the
  branch must be up to date, the tree it tests already holds `main`, so a
  cross-PR interaction (two individually-green PRs
  colliding on a latent bug) is caught on the later PR's own run. THE
  COMPILER IS CACHED BY
  ITS OWN SOURCE (`tools/compiler_paths.sh`): a tree whose compiler is
  main's takes main's binary; otherwise the newest cached binary builds
  the tree twice (the generation law), and one too old to read it — new
  syntax, a new refusal about its own source — fails that build and the
  tree BOOTSTRAPS from the committed seed. Main's own push run caches
  the compiler every run starts from.
- A LANE ITERATES WITH `make try`, NEVER `make avra`: it builds the
  compiler with the STANDING `build/avra` into `build/avra-try` and never
  replaces the builder, so its store stays warm (a leaf edit, ~4 s held
  464/466) and `./avra-try <cmd>` probes the change. `make avra` is for
  a change the compiler must READ to build itself — codegen, the front
  end, a refusal about its own source — and before landing.
- A PRE-COMMIT HOOK refuses staged `.av` that is not canonical; the fix
  it prints is `build/avra fmt --write <files>`. Never `--no-verify`.
- HEAVY RUNS GO ON SPRITES, ONE SPRITE A LANE: `sh tools/work run <cmd>`
  from inside the worktree. `work new` binds a free Sprite (`work bind`
  for a worktree that has none, `work unbind` frees it), and the lane's
  tree and compiler stay warm there between runs. Bootstraps, whole
  suites and censuses run there; the Mac keeps quick targeted checks and
  anything macOS-only. ONE RUN PER SPRITE, EVERY STEP BOUNDED: `run`
  answers the command's status, or 76 (busy), 70 (the compiler does not
  build), 124/125 (a bound; `--for <minutes>` raises the command's), 137
  (out of memory), 75 (the Sprite did not answer), 74 (the provider did
  not answer) — and a failure's last line begins with the one of three
  that failed: SPRITE, CONNECTION or COMMAND. A RUN BELONGS TO THE
  SPRITE, NOT TO THE CONNECTION: a supervisor there keeps its output and
  status and holds the Sprite awake while it lives, `run` only follows
  it, and a dropped connection is followed again from the byte it stood
  at — so Ctrl-C or `work stop` ends a run; a drop, a hangup or the
  client being killed never does (it says so, and the next `run` answers
  76 until `work attach` has followed it out); a run is as long as its
  `--for` says, and the Sprite ends it at its bound whoever is
  watching (`work attach` follows again, `work stop` ends it, `work
  done` ends it with the lane). `sh tools/work sprites` shows all of
  them in seconds.
  A RUN ANSWERS ABOUT THIS WORKTREE OR NOT AT ALL: rsync carries files
  to the Sprite, a file the worktree no longer has is removed there by
  name, and the Sprite's manifest (every path and its hash) must equal
  the worktree's before anything starts — else `SPRITE — sync:` and 75.
  What a run wrote is left: `build/`, `.avra-cache`, anything git ignores.
  WHAT ENDS A RUN EARLY IS MEMORY, NOT TIME: a twenty-minute exec holds,
  chatty or silent, and thirty-two spinning processes leave a Sprite
  answering in a second — but a Sprite says 16 GB and a balloon holds
  half, more while it idles (3.3 to 7.3 GB were free to a run), there is
  no swap, and under about 250 MB the whole machine answers nobody for
  minutes. The Sprite's keeper ends a run at 600 MB (137), and every run
  says what it had to start with. A SPRITE WITH NO SESSION AND NO HOLD
  IS SUSPENDED WITHIN SECONDS, MID-WRITE IF NEED BE, which is why
  nothing runs there detached without the hold; one silent for minutes
  has lost its filesystem and is destroyed and created again
  (provisioning is `run`'s first step, from `.github/ci/packages.txt`).
  WHAT HOLDS A SPRITE AWAKE WITH NOBODY ATTACHED IS ITS TASKS API AND
  NOTHING ELSE WE TRIED, measured over 400 s without contact: a task
  refreshed each minute, no gap; a detached TTY session that prints, no
  gap; a running service, a 372 s gap; outbound traffic, frozen at once;
  an exec from outside every 20 s, one tick each. And a task's name is
  lowercase letters, digits and dashes or the Sprite answers 400 — a
  run is named after the machine that began it, capitals and all, so the
  hold is asked under a name made to fit and ITS ANSWER IS READ. A run
  that stood still says for how long in its own output, and `work
  sprites` shows it beside how long the run has been quiet.
- A BRANCH IS REBASED ONTO `origin/main` ONLY, never onto another
  unlanded branch: that lands the other branch's work unverified. A
  branch built on a stale local main moves with `git rebase --onto
  origin/main main <branch>`, which carries only its own commits.
- A PID IS CHECKED BEFORE IT IS KILLED. A recorded pid is reused once
  its process exits; read `ps -o command= -p <pid>` first.
- A TOOL IS RUN FOR REAL ONCE BEFORE IT BECOMES A DEFAULT. Fixtures
  prove the logic; a live run proves the path (a 62 MB upload hit a
  30 s client timeout that no fixture could reach).
- A GATE FLOOR IS RELATIVE (N − k), NEVER AN ABSOLUTE COUNT: the total
  moves when a branch deletes files, and an absolute floor then fails
  correct work.
- A CHANGE THE COMPILER CHECKS ABOUT ITS OWN SOURCE (a renamed type, a
  new license form) lands as a BRIDGE first: main's compiler must build
  the branch, because the seed and the gate's own build both use it.

## Working discipline

- NOTHING WE RUN TAKES MORE THAN A COUPLE OF MINUTES. Every command,
  build, wait and poll is bounded to ~2 minutes; the ONE exception is a
  full test run, which is ~5 minutes and runs on a Sprite. No `sleep`
  chains, no 10–60 minute timeouts, no loop that polls `main` or a build
  to infer progress. Break work into bounded steps: kick a long job off
  as ONE bounded background command, do useful work, then check ONCE. A
  `work wait` for a landing is bounded to a couple of minutes per call,
  never an hour, and it reads the PR's state, never `main`.
  A lane that blocks for minutes waiting is a defect in the lane, not
  patience. (Owner rule, 2026-10-02: an 18-minute `sleep` loop waiting on
  `main` deadlocked the merge queue — main could not move because that
  lane's own PR was failing the train.)

- GITHUB'S RUNNERS ARE THE ONLY GATE. `tools/gate_changed.sh` is the
  gate's checks in one definition — the static keepers, `fmt --check`
  on the changed `.av`, `check --baseline` on every affected package —
  and checks.yml runs it on every PR, plus the compiler-dependent
  keepers, the seed check and the affected packages' suites.
  `tools/work land`
  checks formatting alone, with the compiler the worktree already
  holds, and asks no other machine; a lane that wants the whole gate
  before pushing runs that script through `work run`.
- A GREEN PR LANDS ITSELF, AND A STALE ONE IS REFRESHED. An armed PR
  that falls behind `main` is updated by the watcher
  (`tools/pr_watcher.py`, `gh pr update-branch`) so "up to date" is met
  without a human; the watcher also arms a green PR, names a conflict
  and cancels a closed PR's run. `work status` shows each PR's check,
  its merge state and whether auto-merge is armed.
- MEASURE, THEN CHANGE. `make census CMD="check <pkg>"` gives EXACT
  retain/release/list-write counts and, with the per-caller tables,
  who causes them; `AVRA_SAMPLE=<secs> sh tools/watch.sh 6000 ./avra
  …` samples. Trust the census over the sample — and read
  `sample`'s output with its tree characters (`+ ! : |`) in mind,
  since parsing it as plain indentation reports the wrong fn.
- A GEN-N VS GEN-N+1 DIVERGENCE IS FOUND BY TRACING, NEVER GUESSED.
  `AVRA_QTRACE=1` prints one stderr line per query-kernel event —
  every `Memo.ask` (family, arg, reuse/compute/cycle) and
  `Memo.settle` (family, arg, fingerprint) in @std/relation's
  engine/answers.av, every
  `Binder.declare` (name, file) in features/namespace.av, every
  failed `named_type` lookup in compiler/typing/declare.av, every
  file a check PARSES (`Q parse <path>`, compiler/program.av), every
  ATTEMPT a derivation makes (`Q attempt <turn> hold … reading <n>`,
  compiler/derive.av) — behind
  `avra_qtrace` (runtime/avra_runtime.c), inert without the flag.
  Run both binaries on the SAME input with `AVRA_QTRACE=1`, confirm
  each is deterministic against itself (diff two runs of the same
  binary — must be empty), then diff the two traces: the FIRST
  differing line names the query whose answer diverged first. Add a
  probe at the divergent query's own site the same way — one
  `qtrace(...)` call, removed once the cause is found.
- WHICH COPY FORKED IS ANSWERED BY A CLONE LOG, NEVER BY READING THE
  MECHANISM'S SOURCE. `AVRA_ALIAS_LOG=1` prints one stderr line per
  ACTUAL `box_clone` (`avra_cell_unique`/`avra_slot_unique`,
  runtime/avra_runtime.c's `alias_log_clone` — box_clone's only two
  callers, so nothing clones outside this log) — the caller's
  unslid return address (`atos -o <binary> <addr>` names it, no
  `-l` needed) and the cloned box's ELEMENT COUNT. THAT COUNT IS
  `a->len`, NEVER the header's `len`: every list, record and enum
  payload is one `AvraArray` shape (`array_clone` treats them so),
  and the header's `len` is that WRAPPER STRUCT's own fixed byte
  size (40, `sizeof(AvraArray)`) — constant regardless of how many
  fields or elements the box holds, so reading it answers "a box
  was cloned" and never "how big". The first draft of this log
  read the header and every clone in a 5.2M-line run showed length
  40 or 32 — a tautology, not a finding.
  AND DIFF THE LOGS BY SITE, NEVER BY PROFILE. avra-2y5c.5's gen-2
  break was read from this log as an acquittal — "the same functions
  at the same counts" in the good run and the broken one — while the
  broken run held ONE line the good one did not: a 44-field clone at
  `CheckCmd.run` (`mut ws = o.ws`, a workspace copied out of a record;
  see A VALUE ITS OWN HOOKS CAPTURE, under Rules). Five million lines
  that agree hide the one that forks.
- A `check` HIT ON `.avra-cache` EXAMINES NOTHING, AND A SECOND

#!/bin/sh
# THE PRE-GATE, on worktree /work/gate-wt of /work/avra. Two steps:
#   sh /work/gate.sh merge <base> [ref|file.bundle:branch]...
#       checks out <base> (a ref, or file.bundle:branch), merges the rest in order;
#       a conflict lists its files and stops (the tree is left mid-merge for a decision).
#   sh /work/gate.sh check [--rc FILE]... [--test FILE]...
#       the full gate on the worktree's HEAD, one heavy job at a time, every build cold,
#       every check as non-root user `gate`; GATE_SEED=<compiler> overrides the standing $src/build/avra. --rc runs AVRA_RC_GUARD=1 over a lone program
#       file (evaluator, native old path, native program layer; output vs its .expected);
#       --test runs `avra test FILE`. Each --rc case is also wrapped as a package for its
#       program-layer row, after a positive control that must abort under the guard. Every tools/witness_program_*.sh is run.
# Prints one table (check | result | detail | wall). Logs in /work/gate-logs/<run>/.
set -u
src=/work/avra
wt=/work/gate-wt
. /etc/profile.d/avra.sh
export AVRA_MEM_CEILING_MB=12000

resolve() { # a ref, or file.bundle:branch fetched into refs/gate/<file>/<branch>
    case $1 in
        *.bundle:*)
            f=${1%%:*}; b=${1#*:}; [ -f "$f" ] || f=/work/$f
            n=$(basename "$f" .bundle)
            git -C "$src" fetch -q "$f" "+refs/heads/*:refs/gate/$n/*" || return 1
            echo "refs/gate/$n/$b" ;;
        *) echo "$1" ;;
    esac
}

if [ "${1:-}" = merge ]; then
    shift
    find "$src/.git" -name '._*' -delete 2>/dev/null
    [ -e "$wt/.git" ] || git -C "$src" worktree add -f --detach "$wt" program >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "gate: worktree add failed"; exit 2; }
    cd "$wt" || exit 2
    git merge --abort 2>/dev/null
    base=$(resolve "$1") || exit 3; shift
    git checkout -q -f --detach "$base" || { echo "gate: checkout $base failed"; exit 2; }
    git clean -q -f -d -e build/ >/dev/null
    echo "base $base = $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"
    for m in "$@"; do
        r=$(resolve "$m") || exit 3
        if git -c user.name=gate -c user.email=gate@localhost merge -q --no-ff --no-edit "$r" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "merged $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) -> $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD)"

            echo "MERGE CONFLICT merging $m ($(git rev-parse --short=8 "$r")) onto $(git rev-parse --short=8 HEAD):"
            git diff --name-only --diff-filter=U | sed 's/^/  /'
            exit 4
        fi
    done
    exit 0

# Avra — clean-room compiler

## AVRA PRINCIPLES

The spec's Part 0 frames every decision (full text: spec, Part 0).
Above all: **P6, paradox collapse** — binary choices are usually false
dichotomies; find the design where both sides win. When a trade-off
feels forced, the model is wrong, not the requirements.

- P1  LLM-first: correct on first generation is the success metric
- P2  substrate for autonomous services
- P3  gloriously declarative, zero ceremony
- P4  Rust-level performance or better
- P5  full-stack vertical integration
- P6  paradox collapse
- P7  visible magic — always inspectable
- P8  escape hatches everywhere
- P9  boundaries are contracts
- P10 the compiler holds semantic knowledge no other tool has
- P11 machine-readability is the substrate, human-readability the projection
- P12 one source of truth, many projections
- P13 collapse dev/ops/infra
- P14 no runtime, no framework, no container
- P17 composability over featurefulness

Clean restart of the Avra compiler, built slowly, one reviewed file at a
time. Front end first: an extensible grammar assembled from
LanguageFeature components, producing an AST for later passes.
Toolchain: the compiler builds itself — `./avra` runs `build/avra`,
and a cold tree bootstraps from `bootstrap/seed.ll.gz` (`make bootstrap`;
README.md).

Design sources of truth (in `../forge-crafting-intepreters`):
- `docs/2026_04_18_FULL_SPEC.md` — the language
- `docs/2026_06_14_AST_SOURCE_OF_TRUTH_EPIC.md` — node model, spans, error tolerance
- `bootstrap/docs/2026_08_19_STANDARDIZATION.md` — front-end shape

Follow the old tree's *documented designs*, never its code habits.

## Comments

Never write comments about specific situations, tickets, approaches, or
points in time. Comments are evergreen: always relevant, or absent.
Keep them very terse, in plain language. State what a thing is or the
invariant it holds — no narration, no self-justification, no history.

## The idiom bar — BEFORE writing any fn

First drafts are written idiomatic, not cleaned up later. Before
the body exists, answer:

1. Is any loop a MAP/FILTER/FLAT-MAP? Comprehension (`?` works in
   element and iterable; predicates hoist into named fns).
2. Building head-plus-tail? `concat` (a list METHOD) / `flatten`
   (core's FREE fn — `flatten(xs)`, never `xs.flatten()`), never
   push-ceremony.
3. Is a projection being spelled twice? The second spelling names a
   verb (`cx.int_at`, `expr_fps`) or uses the existing one.
4. Does absence read straight? (`?? `, `?.`, if-null early return —
   never a two-arm null match without payload logic on both arms.)
5. Scanning for one element? `find`/`any`/`index_of`, not a flag
   loop.
6. Unsure a shape compiles in the subset? PROBE in scratch first —
   fear of traps is how ugly-but-safe drafts happen, and every
   probe result gets recorded so the fear shrinks.

DOGFOODING.md is the full rulebook; `avra check --baseline
tools/idioms.baseline` FAILS on any NEW site — the baseline lists
sites, never counts, and no tool path can add to it (`make idioms`
runs every package, `make idioms-accept` prunes what a fix made
gone). Every idiom the language can state is a `rule` declaration,
found by `avra check` itself, and the gate counts a RULE's finding
only — `type.alias_copy` wears the same `warning[kind]` shape and is
the compiler's own law, never a rule, so the gate reads the rule
table (`avra rules --json`), never a kind-string shape. Accepted
debt lives in the baseline alone, reviewed at adoption and every
time after. A new idiom lands in DOGFOODING's registry AT DISCOVERY,
named by its rule — `<module>.<rule>`, never a number.

## Style

- Inline single-use values. A `let` earns its place only when the
  name carries meaning the expression lacks, the value is read more
  than once, or the subset REQUIRES a pin (a `dyn` value selected
  among arms, a Result-answering lambda — "The subset today" names
  each). Empty literals (`[]`, `{}`) infer inline in
  constructor fields — never bind them to a throwaway name. When a
  pin seems needed, probe before assuming.
- A state struct's impl is its VOCABULARY: the small verbs that
  read or write its tables (`speak`, `bind`, `mint`, `give`) live
  as methods, so drivers read as prose. The free state fns the
  bootstrap habit left (`eval_node(ev, cx, e)`, the interpreter's
  `put(m, …)`, the backend's `define(em, …)`) are methods now, and
  so are the pass contexts' whole vocabularies (`cx.accepts(e,
